Kenny McKinley is the career leader in receptions (207), receiving yards (2,781) and consecutive games with a reception (43) The 23-year-old, second-year pro has been on the team's injured reserve list since early August with a knee injury. He is survived by a young son.

Carrie Fisher suffered a heart attack on a flight from London to L.A. on Dec. 23. She died four days later. Fisher is most widely known for her role as Princess Leia in the Star Wars films. She was also an acclaimed author renowned for her trenchant wit.

A poll from Morning Consult asked 2,200 people to pick their favorite Star Wars character. Leia led the list with a 73 percent favorability rating. Jar Jar Binks finished ahead of Mace Windu, Kylo Ren, Emperor Palpatine, Jyn Erso. Supreme Leader Snoke bottomed out on the list at 26 percent.

A computer model has found a smiling expression is key to a first impression of being approachable. Large eyes signal youthfulness, and dominance is linked partly to a masculine face shape. These findings could lead to computer programs that automatically see which photographs would help people give the best first impressions they can.

Groupon priced its IPO last night at $20 a share and started trading this morning around $30. At $30 a share, Groupon's valuation is about $20 billion. If the next few quarters are as rough as I think they might be, the stock could easily trade down to ~$8 billion.

Lucky Whitehead was wrongly implicated in a shoplifting arrest in Virginia last month. The incident led the team to drop him just hours after a training camp practice Monday. Here is the transcript of the back-and-forth between the media and coach Jason Garrett. Garrett: We made a decision yesterday that we felt was in the best interest of the Dallas Cowboys.

Google's security bounty programs can be quite lucrative for those who discover problems. The company has just published a report looking back at the security landscape in 2015. The report reveals the financial rewards that have been paid out in the last 12 months. In all, Google has paid out more than $2 million to more than 300 people.

The sign outside Treats Family Restaurant in Lonsdale, Minnesota, reads “Muslims Get Out.” A man stabbed several people at a St. Cloud mall, allegedly asking victims if they were Muslim before attacking them. Restaurant owner Dan Ruedinger says the sign has led to some backlash, but he says business is up.

"I don't think it's relevant," former Chief U.S. District Judge Vaughn Walker says of his sexuality. Walker, 67, retired from the bench at the end of February after 21 years. His most prominent ruling was his August decision overturning Proposition 8. Walker is returning to private law practice as head of a San Francisco firm.

There were 1.4 million new cases of diabetes in 2014, a drop from 1.7 million in 2008. It's the first time in a quarter century there's been a significant decline, the CDC reported. About 21.9 million Americans now live with the disease.

Bolivia has rejected an “offensive” donation of 100,000 chickens from Bill Gates. “How can he think we are living 500 years ago, in the middle of the jungle not knowing how to produce?” said César Cocaric, the country’s minister of development. Gates announced the chicken initiative earlier this month.

Bodies of three members of the same family recovered from crushed car. They were the last people reported missing from Tuesday's tragedy. A 200m section of the Morandi bridge suddenly fell 45m, along with dozens of vehicles. The collapse has led to a fierce debate about Italy's infrastructure.

"All the inmates are sick of Lindsay," a relative of an inmate says. "It's almost like Lindsay Lohan's here, but she's not," the relative adds. Lohan is serving a 90-day sentence for violating her probation. She is expected to be released as early as next week.

MongoDB CEO Max Schireson stepped down after asking himself how he can balance the dual demands of fatherhood and running a company. Women are still the focus of the “having it all’ debate and questions of whether or not they can be wildly successful at both jobs.

New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie and former Arkansas Gov. Mike Huckabee are the first casualties of the winnowing GOP presidential debate field. Fox Business Network announced Thursday night that they both officially missed the cut for next week’s contest. They’ll instead participate in the undercard debate, a demotion that could serve as a major blow for their campaigns.

Clippers beat Warriors 113-103 to take 3-2 series lead. Fans wore T-shirts with pictures of Sterling's face crossed out. "We are home!" the fist-pumping DJ bellowed over deep bass. "It's a great day," said Clippers star Chris Paul.

A Playmobil figurine resembles an African American slave wearing a neck shackle. The toy’s instruction manual shows a dark-skinned doll wearing no shoes, ripped pants and a tattered yellow shirt. The set retails for $89.99 but the store is selling it for $62.99. The Sacramento NAACP President Stephen Webb said he wants the toy banned.

The older of the two boys was found Monday morning after authorities received a 911 call. The boy was covered in cuts and scrapes and appeared to have been outside for an extended period. "They went through a pure hell, no doubt," says Ouachita County Sheriff's Detective Lt. Nathan Greeley.

Spamhaus, a group based in both London and Geneva, is a non-profit organisation. It aims to help email providers filter out spam and other unwanted content. Spamhaus blocked servers maintained by Cyberbunker, a Dutch web host. Experts worry the row could escalate to affect banking and email systems. Five national cyber-police-forces are investigating the attacks.

Archaeologists had been looking for San Marcos, one of several forts built on the Santa Elena settlement. The location was nailed down using radar and magnetometers. Traditional digging methods had failed to find the fort. The fort was founded in 1577 by Pedro Menendez Marquez.

Keith Olbermann named Florida Rep. Brad Drake as one of his “Worst Persons In The World’ for sponsoring legislation to replace lethal injection as a execution method with electrocution or by firing squad. Drake said the idea came to him after having a conversation with a constituent at a Waffle House over the legal battles associated with the Sept. 28 execution of Manuel Valle. The GOP-controlled Florida Legislature will consider the bill during the 2012 session.

Two officials in southern Guangdong Province were found purchasing corpses from grave robbers. They were trying to meet government cremation quotas, Chinese media reported last week. China has a long tradition of ancestor worship, which usually requires families bury their relatives. The Chinese government has encouraged cremations to save land for farming and development.

The Obama administration announced Tuesday it would delay enforcing a provision of the new health-care law. The law requires large employers to provide coverage for workers or pay a penalty in 2014. The delay, announced by the Treasury Department in a blog post Tuesday, means that penalty won't kick in until 2015.

Online dating is the second most common way for heterosexual couples to meet. For homosexual couples, it is far and away the most popular. Loose ties have traditionally played a key role in meeting partners. When people meet in this way, it sets up social links that were previously nonexistent.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad said he plans to visit North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Since taking power in 2011, Kim has not publicly met with another head of state in North Korea. Both countries have faced international isolation, North Korea over its nuclear weapons program, and Syria over its tactics during a bloody civil war.

Cruz mocks Biden, then apologizes The joke had been a winner in the past for the Texas Republican. Biden's eldest son, Beau, died Saturday of brain cancer. "It was a mistake to use an old joke about Joe Biden during his time of grief," Cruz said.

The Leonid meteor shower will hit its peak Tuesday, November 17. The annual event is caused by bits of ice and rock burning in Earth’s atmosphere. NASA predicts we’ll see one meteor about every four minutes. The Leonids peak every three decades, and this shower comes mid-cycle.

The 552-carat yellow gem was found at the Diavik mine in the Northwest Territories. It is almost three times the size of the next largest stone ever found in Canada. Yellow stones typically sell at a discount to Type IIa top whites often found in the best African mines.

Long-time Hubbard, Ohio, residents Rick and Cindy Krlich say everyone in their town has turned against them. Over the past seven years, they said, horns have been honked 5,000 times by people driving past their house. Watch ABC News' "20/20? on Friday, May 2 at 10 p.m. ET to see what happened.

Kim Jong-un is the third and youngest son of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il. He has been appointed a four-star general, despite having no military experience. His elder brother and half-brother appear to have been ruled out of the running. Kim is said to be suffering from several illnesses and is in China for treatment.

NEW: 150 sets of DNA have been recovered from the crash site. Andreas Lubitz researched suicide methods on the Internet, a German prosecutor says. The flight data recorder is found about 8 inches (20 centimeters) below the surface. Lubitz is suspected of deliberately bringing down Germanwings Flight 9525.

About 80% of the migrants are from Honduras. Many said they are fleeing poverty, but also violence that followed the swearing in of Honduran President Juan Orlando Hernández after a highly contested election last year. The number of people who showed up to travel with the caravan caught organizers by surprise.

Mel B says she was emotionally weak when she married Stephen Belafonte. She says he destroyed her self-confidence and self-esteem, especially because she was struggling to lose her pregnancy weight. In December 2014, she tried committing suicide by swallowing an entire bottle of Aspirin. Mel B says what finally gave her the push was her father dying.

Kris Maharaj, 75, has spent 27 years in a Florida prison for a double murder that they say he did not commit. His lawyers have released details of the 53 witnesses and 498 documents they plan to call on in the hope of persuading a judge to order a retrial. The newly released documents underline the massive case for exoneration that has been built up by Maharaj’s lawyers.

Posters show Meryl Streep next to Harvey Weinstein with a red strip across her face with the text “She knew,” an apparent reference to Weinstein’s alleged sexual abuse of women over the course of decades. The posters are a riff on the work of artist Barbara Kruger, whose signature text in red banners has been adapted and copied for decades.

Lizandra Cosme, 32, of Chicago, was arrested Sunday and charged with five counts of aggravated battery of a child under 13 years old causing great bodily harm. Susana D. Gonzalez, 27, of Melrose Park, was charged with 5 misdemeanor counts of causing the circumstances of child endangerment, police said. Three girls and two boys were hurt in the incident, but the extent of their injuries is unclear. The Department of Children and Family Services said it is investigating the incident.

Burberry announces it will stop destroying unsaleable products, with immediate effect. Burberry also confirms it will no longer use real fur. There will be no real fur in Riccardo Tisci’s debut collection for Burberry later this month, and we will phase out existing real fur products.

Benny Anders was a swingman for the Houston Cougars in the 1980s. He once threw down a vicious dunk in a Final Four game against Louisville. Anders never made as big an impact again and failed to ascend to the NBA. "Where in the world is Benny Anders?" became a parlor game in hoops ecosystem.

President Trump says he is open to a path to citizenship for some "dreamers" But his support of a citizenship path would be contingent on securing $25 billion for a wall. The president also is expected to continue his push to curb legal immigration as part of a deal. The impasse over immigration led to a brief, partial government shutdown.

Legend has it that the Hope diamond brings misfortune to whoever owns it. The most commonly accepted origin of the curse dates back to 1653. The diamond has changed hands many times, and for a few periods in its life, the name of the owner is lost to history. Today the sky-blue gem is worth a quarter of a billion dollars.

Right-of-center websites are promoting a new video of leaked raw footage that alleges “proof” that CBS’ Evening News anchor Katie Couric was mocking then Alaska Governor Sarah Palin on the day she was announced as John McCain’s running mate. But what evidence is there that she was making fun of Palin? Not much.

The RQ-180 is scheduled to enter production for the U.S. Air Force and could be operational by 2015. The aircraft will conduct the penetrating ISR mission that has been left unaddressed since 1998. The new UAS underpins the Air Force’s determination to retire a version of the R Q-4B Global Hawk after 2014.

Scientists shed new light on a massive solar storm that narrowly missed impacting Earth two years ago. The solar storm, which happened on July 23, 2012, was the strongest one ever recorded. If we had been in its path, NASA says it would have had a "catastrophic effect"

Chris and Dana White from Pensacola were staying aboard the Carnival Fantasy for a three-day Caribbean cruise from Mobile, Alabama to Mexico last October. They say they discovered a recording device hidden among TV wires in their stateroom. The couple immediately called security and Chris took a video of an employee on the ship inspecting the device and taking it apart. The device was given to the FBI for further inspection.

Thomas Keith Henderson, 56, of Elkhorn was arrested and charged with DUI (CDL) and Defective Equipment. The sheriff's department says Henderson's blood alcohol level was 0.09. That's more than twice the 0.04 legal limit for commercial driver's license holders. Henderson is employed by the West Virginia Department of Transportation.

A video that features ants crawling over a crucifix has gone on display at a New York gallery. The video was banned from a Smithsonian museum. It has renewed opposition from religious groups offended by the depiction of Jesus covered by insects. "I think that in the artistic community, directors, curators are tremendously insensitive to Christians," says Catholic League President Bill Donohue.

Vladimir Katriuk was No. 2 on the Simon Wiesenthal Center’s list of most wanted Nazi war criminals. His lawyer said his client had been ill for a long time before his recent death at the age of 93. The Russian Embassy in Ottawa ripped into the federal government Thursday.

Twenty-two states and D.C. are backing Montana in its fight to keep a ban on corporate campaign spending. The Supreme Court is being asked to reverse a state court's decision to uphold the Montana law. Critics hope the court will reverse itself on the controversial Citizens United ruling. Legal observers say don't count on the Supreme Court reconsidering its decision.

Minnesota Rep. Michele Bachmann has requested withdrawal of her Swiss citizenship. Bachmann said she was withdrawing the citizenship to make clear her allegiance to the U.S. She had initially tried to downplay the citizenship, calling it a “non-story’ Bachmann's DFL challenger Jim Graves called news that Bachmann had sought to register her Swiss citizen a "distraction"

The NYPD says the subway surfer who was videotaped riding on the outside of a C train last week has been arrested. And this was at least the third time he's been caught doing so, leading one to wonder: does he know something we don't know? Isaiah Thompson, 22, was arrested on Tuesday and has been charged with reckless endangerment and disorderly conduct.

Crawl of outlinks from wikipedia.org started March, 2016. These files are currently not publicly accessible. It has been several years since the last time we did this. This collection will be complete, as there is a good chance we will share the data.

At least 717 people have been killed in a stampede near Mecca, officials say. Another 863 people were injured in the incident at Mina. It is the deadliest incident to occur during the Hajj in 25 years. King Salman has ordered an urgent review of this year's Hajj plans.

Porn star and escort Devon James is claiming Tiger Woods fathered her secret love child. James, 29, gave birth to her son in early 2001, before Woods and Elin Nordegren were married. James is one of approximately 15 women linked to Woods, 34, in secret sexual affairs. A source familiar with the situation told RadarOnline.com that Tiger has not taken a paternity test.

Gates and his wife Melinda have emerged as two of history’s most powerful philanthropists. The Gates Foundation has an endowment of $42 billion, almost four times the size of the Ford Foundation. Gates releases his annual letter each January, laying out its priorities for the coming year.

Politico: Top Republicans are increasingly vocal about their long-held belief that Speaker Paul Ryan will wind up as the nominee. One of the nation’s best-wired Republicans, with an enviable prediction record, sees a 60 percent chance of a convention deadlock and a 90 percent chance that delegates turn to Ryan.

Divers found two more bodies early Friday, raising the death toll from 11 to 13. Missouri State Highway Patrol Sgt. Jason Pace said four people remain missing. The Ride the Ducks boat sank on Table Rock Lake in Branson Thursday evening. Another duck boat on the lake made it safely back to shore.

Kenneth Burke, 46, and Timothy Foote, 38, of Ocean Township, called for a taxi to a home. They instructed the taxi driver to wait outside before they returned, police say. The driver then took them to an apartment in Asbury Park, where they got out without paying the fare. The stolen goods were later returned to the homeowner, police said.

The driver of a tractor-trailer that went over the side of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel died after being rescued. Authorities identified the driver as 47-year-old Joseph Chen, of Greenville, North Carolina. Chen was hauling a load of seafood for Evans Transports. The Medical Examiner’s Office ruled Chen's death to be accidental. The cause was drowning and hypothermia.

Uber Technologies Inc., the car-sharing service that’s rankling cabbies across the U.S., is fighting its biggest protest from European drivers. Traffic snarled in cities from London to Madrid and Berlin to Paris as strikes and gatherings by more than 30,000 taxi and limo drivers blocked tourist centers and shopping districts. They are asking regulators to apply tougher rules on San Francisco-based Uber.

Diego caused quite a stir last week when a video taken shortly after he was born went viral. The video has garnered 12 million views and more than 138,000 shares since Thursday. Protestors have not only shared their displeasure at seeing a baby animal they believe will soon be slaughtered, but have used Facebook’s starring system to drive down the farm's reviews.

The FDA is aware of at least six reports between 1998 and 2009 of serious injury or death, including three deaths in the United States and one in Canada. The Lifeline pendant button is intentionally designed to not break away when tugged, which prevents the button from accidentally falling off. There are more than 750,000 users of these devices in the U.S. and Canada.

Whistled languages, although unusual, have been around for centuries. Most of the forty-two examples that have been documented in recent times arose in places with steep terrain or dense forests. In recent years, the town of Kuşköy has organized a whistling contest to encourage cultural preservation.

Dominique Strauss-Kahn has been placed in a wing with about 14 cells, all of which are empty except for his. He has his cell to himself, and there is a toilet and sink in the cell. The 62-year-old banker and diplomat has a whole jail wing to himself. Guards checking him 24 hours a day to make sure he doesn't kill himself.

A new study found that only 39 of 100 psychology studies could be replicated. That could mean that the studies were wrong in the first place. But researchers say that the findings tell more about the difficulty of designing a reproducible study than the accuracy of the studies themselves. The study being published today speaks to why a bigger focus on reproducibility is necessary.

Santa Ono, president of the University of Cincinnati, said he twice tried to kill himself. Ono: "There's light at the end of the tunnel. If you have the proper counseling and support, it's really possible for you to move past that and move back into functioning life" A university official said Ono was instrumental in finding resources for UC to provide any student with five free sessions of mental health counseling.

Del. David Yancey's lawyer said that was the first time in Virginia that an election result had been changed in a recount. A lawyer for the Virginia House Democratic caucus said that the local court’s decision about the ballot was wrong. Tied votes, which are extremely rare, have occasionally been broken around the country by coin tosses.

NEW: Massachusetts General Hospital says it received 13 patients between ages 16 and 19. NEW: Most patients had a problem with dehydration, drugs and alcohol, authorities say. Avicii, the Swedish artist behind the hit song "Wake Me Up," performed at the TD Garden. A man collapsed and died after leaving the Electric Daisy Carnival in Las Vegas.

Burger King is testing the Whopperito, a burger-tortilla hybrid. The Whopperrito is currently available at a Burger King in Hermitage, Pennsylvania. It’s unclear if the Whoppersito will hit stores in other cities or states, but that hasn’t stopped potential customers from discussing the item.

China calls on the U.S. to bar a Taiwanese delegation from attending Donald Trump's inauguration. Taiwan delegation, led by former premier and ex-ruling party leader Yu Shyi-kun, will attend. China considers Taiwan a breakaway province, with no right to have diplomatic relations with other countries.

President Tommy Remengesau says he wants to encourage high-end hotels that “would come in with their own designed water treatment system [and] power back-ups” He says it's also about developing the islands in a way that respects the natural environment and those who call the country home.

The court, in a 6-2 ruling, was unpersuaded by arguments from two Maine men. The dispute drew interest from advocates for victims of domestic abuse. Gun rights groups argued that the men should not lose their constitutional right to bear arms. A federal appeals court ruled against the men.

Nigeria's military says it has raided a Boko Haram intelligence unit. The cell leader Babuji Ya'ari was arrested, a military statement said. More than 2,000 people have been killed this year in attacks blamed on Boko Haram. Boko Haram militants abducted more than 200 girls from their school in Borno state.

Russia's track and field team is barred from competing in the Olympic Games this summer. The International Association of Athletics Federations announced the decision Friday. Not even East Germany, which conducted a notorious doping scheme throughout the 1960s, ’70s and ’80s, faced such a penalty. Individual athletes can apply to compete as a neutral athlete.

David Rothkopf: Obama should reconvene Congress and put this one before them. He says it might help the Administration figure out what, exactly, it hopes to accomplish by shooting missiles in the general direction of Damascus. He asks: If the Administration can’t stand up to Ted Cruz, it can hardly hope to frighten Bashar al-Assad. Rothkapf: The Administration needs Congress to laid out what it thinks is going to look like on a personal level.

A Christmas carol service in Sri Lanka mistakenly supplied the lyrics to the Tupac Shakur song, Hail Mary, instead of those of the traditional Christian prayer. Pictures of the programme from Joy to the World 2016, one of Sri Lanka’s largest carol services, were shared widely across social media over the Christmas weekend.

Khaled A. Shabani, 46, was arrested at Ruby's Salon in Madison, Wisconsin. The 22-year-old customer had gone to the salon to get his hair cut. He claimed ShabANI began complaining he was fidgeting and moving his head, and twisted his ear. The man called police when he got home, and Sh Kabani was arrested.

Trevor Story has six home runs and 11 RBI in his first 19 major-league at-bats. "I don't think I've ever seen anything like it, let alone a rookie," manager Walt Weiss says. "He's fearless. He's playing like a Hall of Famer right now," Rockies slugger Carlos Gonzalez says. The Padres were outscored 25-0 while getting swept by the Dodgers.

A video parody of Donald Trump's presidential bid uses Game of Thrones as a backdrop. The clip uses real Trump footage and speech audio and merges it almost seamlessly with key scenes. It shows Trump negotiating with Littlefinger, facing down the queen of dragons, Daenerys Targaryen, and even preparing for battle alongside Tyrion Lannister.

Large Libyan military convoy arrives in Niger: source. "There are persistent rumours that Kadhafi or one of his sons are travelling in the convoy," the source said. A journalist from a private radio station in Agadez said he saw "a convoy of several dozen vehicles crossing the city and heading towards Niamey", the Niger capital.

Jonathan Trappe left Caribou, Maine, on Thursday in a small boat suspended below more than 300 helium-filled balloons. Trappe said he was burning through ballast too quickly to make it across the Atlantic. He was forced to choose between landing in the isolated woods Thursday night or ditching over the ocean sometime Friday.

Jason Van Dyke now works for the Fraternal Order of Police, the union president says. He makes $12 an hour to be a jack-of-all-trades for the union, Dean Angelo says. The Rev. Michael Pfleger blasted the move, saying in a Facebook post: “The Police Union says to Chicago we don’t give a Damn what he did or what you think he is one of ours”

"The Putin Interviews" might be the most high-stakes documentary Showtime has ever aired. Oliver Stone and Vladimir Putin's dynamic has a hint of slapstick comedy. Stone is less invested in investigating Putin than he is in re-narrativizing the history of American dominance.

The Clarion Nightsnake was found on the Pacific island of Clarion in Mexico. The snake was first discovered in 1936 by naturalist William Beebe. Although never declared extinct, it was struck from the record after scientists were unable to rediscover it. DNA tests confirmed that the snake was genetically distinct from others found in mainland Mexico.

Domingo Moreno, 27, of Parsippany, is facing criminal mischief, tampering with evidence. He allegedly crashed a 1999 Nissan Quest into a mailbox and a fire hydrant. Police followed a fluid trail from the crash site to a residence on Norman Avenue. Moreno was located at a nearby diner and placed under arrest.

Eighty-eight-year-old Gene Warrington, 86, and his wife, Pat, died Dec. 27 in Findlay, Ohio. "You could have almost predicted it," said their son, Phil. "They did everything in their life together. They were never apart" The couple raised three children and had seven grandchildren and a dozen great-grandchildren.

Sen. Saxby Chambliss (R-GA) will retire in 2014 rather than seek a third term. Former presidential candidate Herman Cain would be a strong contender, but he said again Friday that he is not running. Former Georgia Secretary of State Karen Handel was also interested in the race. Atlanta Mayor Kasim Reed is considered a top Democratic prospect.

"Swamp People" is a ratings win for The History Channel in its Thursday night timeslot. The series is set in Louisiana's Atchafalaya Swamp, and focuses on Cajun alligator hunters. Last week, "Swamps People" was the top original cable program, pulling in 3.8 million viewers.

Mohammed Ghannouchi is seen as being too close to former President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali. He was speaking at a news conference in Tunis, after making a lengthy speech defending his record in government. "I am not ready to be the person who takes decisions that would end up causing casualties," he said.

Muslim community has condemned violence and distanced itself from the suspects. Investigators are working to uncover whether the suspects, Chechen-American Muslim brothers, were lone assailants or trained by a terrorist organization. Tamerlan Tsarnaev, the older of the two, has been described as more attuned to radical Islamic movements.

Sen. Ralph Shortey, R-Oklahoma City, is charged with three felony counts. He is accused of offering to pay a 17-year-old boy for sex. The two met through a Craigslist personal encounter, according to a court affidavit. The state Senate on Wednesday voted to punish Shortey for "disorderly behavior"

Authorities are looking for 23-year-old Jesus Henry Kong, also known as Jessie Eloah Calix and Jesus Matute. Officials say he has a "history of law enforcement encounters" and is a transient who has lived in Florida, California, Virginia and Maryland. The threats started on July 24 and have targeted William R. Boone High School, Edgewater High School and Colonial High School.

Life expectancy is on the rise for the poor in Birmingham, Alabama, but in Tampa, Florida, the poor are on the downslide when it comes to life expectancy. "I would have thought these very expensive big cities, like New York City and San Francisco, for most poor would be stressful and would be places with poor health," Chetty said.

The UK election results mean stable global markets ... for now. The British pound was rising versus all major global currencies. The Scottish National Party swelled from a cottage party to the third largest elected power in parliament. Cameron has promised the country a referendum in 2017 on whether to stay in the EU.

Tearful radio hosts say sorry to nurse's family in UK. 2Day FM's owner said it was cancelling their show and stopping all hoax calls by its broadcasters. DJs Mel Greig and Michael Christian have been in hiding and undergoing counselling. The hoax sparked global outrage following the apparent suicide of Jacintha Saldanha.

Jon Favreau: A vote to raise the debt limit will not cost taxpayers a single dime. He says a failure to raise debt limit would inflict far more pain on far more people than a government shutdown. The White House should keep using the phrase “economic shutdown,” Favreau says.

Strauss-Kahn and Nafissatou Diallo have reached an agreement, a person says. A confidentiality agreement likely will prevent the two from speaking publicly. A court date is expected next week, though the day wasn't set, the person said. The deal comes after prosecutors dropped related criminal charges last year.

British Royal Marine David Hart, 23, was killed by a Taliban bomb while on patrol in Helmand province. He took out a £250,000 life insurance policy before he was deployed. stipulated that $150,000 of that amount should go toward a Las Vegas holiday for his pals and their girlfriends. Family and friends have also planned to embark on a charitable U.K. bike ride to raise money in Hart's memory.

NEW: Prime Minister Abhisit Vejjajiva says the measure is effective in Bangkok and nearby provinces. NEW: Deputy Prime Minister Suthep Thuagsuban has been appointed to administer the emergency law. The emergency allows authorities to take actions without court orders. The cabinet met to extend the country's Internal Security Act for another two weeks.

Wati was 8 when a tsunami hit Indonesia's Aceh in December 2004. For years, the family believed the girl had drowned in the water. Yet on Wednesday, the 15-year-old returned home alive, according to reports. She reportedly did not remember her parents' or relatives' names, except for one.

Oklahoma department of corrections is in dispute with the city of McAlester over who owns the state’s unwired electric chair. State law allows for the electric chair or a firing squad to be used only if lethal injection is found to be unconstitutional. The chair, first used in 1915, was used to execute 82 inmates before it was retired.

Jason Behrens took his kids on vacation and drove through Kearney, Nebraska. The kids became nervous when they noticed the car swerving and making a lot of close calls. After nearly getting into a head on collision, they started sending texts to 911. Kearney Police caught up with the family at a Burger King.

As of January 9, 2019, 62 people infected with the outbreak strain of E. coli O157:H7 were reported from 16 states and the District of Columbia. Illnesses started on dates ranging from October 7, 2018, to December 4, 2018. Ill people reported eating different types of romaine lettuce in several restaurants and at home.

Marvel Studios and director Joe Johnston want to be really sure they’ve found the right actor to star in The First Avenger: Captain America. Of the original contenders, two are still in serious contention: Mike Vogel (Cloverfield) and Garrett Hedlund (Tron: Legacy)

China gained almost 100 million smokers between 1980 and 2012, despite an overall decrease in smoking prevalence in the same period from 30.4 percent to 24.2 percent. China had the highest number of smokers in the world in 2012 with 281 million, about one-third of the world’s smoking population. Average number of cigarettes consumed daily per smoker in China has increased.

David Leonhardt: A new study says Republicans are happier than Democrats. He says the study was done by Brad Wilcox of the right-wing Institute for Family Studies. But even Wilcox admits that causality might work in the opposite direction. Leonhardt says party ID doesn’t seem likely to play a huge role as a causal factor.

Kaiser researchers found no new HIV infections among the more than 650 people they followed over nearly three years. Truvada, a daily pill that holds the hope of eliminating the risk of contracting HIV, appears to be living up to its promise. The study suggests that HIV is very close to being managed like any other chronic disease, such as diabetes or asthma.

The Tahoma Dam was inspected by an engineer and officials determined that the landslide had compromised its integrity. "Act now to preserve your life," urged a tweet from the National Weather Service office in Greenville-Spartanburg, South Carolina.

House Speaker John Boehner (R-Ohio) asked President Obama to address a joint-session of Congress on Thursday, Sept. 8, when it wouldn't conflict with the Republican presidential debate. The White House accepted the Speaker's offer Wednesday night. Boehner accused the White House of ignoring “decades, if not centuries” of protocol on such events.

Police sources say they have a "person of interest" in custody in connection with a string of fake bombs planted across Staten Island. Investigators believe that "hoax devices" were left in Port Richmond, Randall Manor and Grymes Hill as part of a grudge between the two men. The suspect, whose name was not released, is being questioned at the 121st Precinct stationhouse. Charges are pending.

Bart Palosz, 15, committed suicide in August 2013 after the first day of his sophomore year at Greenwich High School. His family is suing Greenwich and the town's school district for $15,000 in damages. The family alleges school officials knew their son was relentlessly bullied for years and failed to protect him.

French economist Thomas Piketty has turned down the Legion of Honor. He says the government should focus on reviving the country’s anemic economy. The economist was once close to the Socialist Party but has distanced himself from the policies of President Francois Hollande. His book examines income inequality in society and became a surprise hit.

Donations of more than $110,000 (£67,000) have poured in for a Boston homeless man. Glen James alerted police after he found the backpack containing cash and traveller's cheques. A complete stranger later started an online fund for Mr James after reading media reports about his honesty.

Google releases a series of photos and videos about its Project Glass headset. The photos show more about how Glass works than any photo of the hardware could convey. Commanding the headset is as easy as uttering the words "OK, Glass" Google is letting a larger segment of the public test its futuristic eyeglasses.

Ross Cassidy met Mr Skripal when he moved in next door in Salisbury in 2010. The haulage contractor got to know Sergei, his wife Lyudmila, his son Alexandr (who was known as Sasha) and Yulia. Mr Cassidy, 61, has spent many hours with counter-terror detectives investigating the poisoning, but would not discuss the police operation.

Community members in Richmond, Indiana, came together at a candlelight vigil Sunday to support the mom of a teenage boy who alerted police. The mother called 911 Thursday to alert authorities "to the imminent danger," the Indiana State Police said. Her actions "likely prevented a lot of lost lives," police said. The armed 14-year-old died at Dennis Intermediate School from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Cain received 37 percent of the 2,600 delegate votes, more than twice as many as Perry. Perry made by far the most extensive effort but finished a distant second with 15 percent. Romney was followed by former Sen. Rick Santorum of Pennsylvania with 11 percent. Paul beat out seven other candidates and "undecided"

Oliver Stone announced Monday that he plans to adapt "The Snowden Files: The Inside Story of the World's Most Wanted Man" The project pairs one of cinema's most controversial directors with one of the most explosive news events in recent years. Sony Pictures last month purchased the big-screen rights to Glenn Greenwald's "No Place to Hide"

Charlie Sheen was outspoken about his belief that 9/11 was a conspiracy. Mark Dice, a prominent member of The 9-11 Truth Movement, tells us his fellow conspiracy theorists are pissed. Mark says he's reached out to Charlie -- to no avail. He tells us if Charlie doesn't address the issue soon, he and several theorists will protest in front of Sheen's shows.

In Venezuela, officials expected roughly 70 cases of Guillain-Barré from December 2015 to the end of March 2016. Instead, there were 684 cases. In Colombia, officials recorded 320 cases when there should have been about 100. Roughly 500 million people in Latin America and the Caribbean are at risk for Zika virus infection.

New Year Brings Minimum-Wage Hikes In 10 States. In Rhode Island, it took a state law to raise the minimum wage for the first time in five years. Washington state has bumped its wage up to $9.19 an hour. Some 40 states will look at raising their minimum wage this year.

Lumos is a charity dedicated to closing child institutions and so-called orphanages. The charity estimates that the institutionalisation of children can be eradicated globally by 2050 – in our lifetime. The solution is investment in education and social support for vulnerable families. The good news is that this is an entirely solvable problem.

Some 20 million Americans are using dating sites, more than double the number five years ago. While they are finding casual dates, they are also encountering married people pretending to be single or, worse, sexual predators and convicted felons. A nascent crop of companies wants to help you find out by running background checks on potential flames.

Police responded to a report of a gunshot victim Thursday morning around 10:45 a.m. Police said the shooting that happened in the 300 block of East Washington Street started with an argument. A witness said he heard the two people in a local barbershop arguing over whether or not Halle Berry played or would play Aretha Franklin in a movie.

Nancy Reed died Sept. 15 of necrotizing fasciitis, according to the Harris County Institute of Forensic Science. The dangerous skin condition resulted in complications related to "blunt trauma of an upper extremity" Reed was a widowed community volunteer who lived in Kingwood, a northern suburb of Houston.

U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry condemns Russia's "invasion and occupation" Putin says Russia reserves the right to defend its interests and people in Crimea. Ukraine's acting president says any Russian military intervention would lead to war. Russia's Parliament signs off on Putin's request to send military forces into Ukraine.

Students at Ethan Chase Middle School in Menifee were encouraged to wear Disney costumes for spirit day on Thursday. Austin Lacey, 13, chose to dress as Elsa from the movie "Frozen" The eighth-grader told KTLA that his classmates loved the idea and asked him to pose for selfies. But, the school principal apparently felt it was inappropriate and told him to take off the costume.

Cameras were rolling Wednesday when a sinkhole opened up underneath the National Corvette Museum in Bowling Green, Ky. Eight of the iconic sports cars were sucked down into a hole about 40 feet deep. The museum has now posted videos of the hole opening up, the cars disappearing and what it looks like inside the pit.

French entrepreneur Margaux Sainte-Lagüe sells hand-painted cobblestones from Paris. The city of Paris began selling thousands of tons of cobblestone as part of its circular economy. Mon Pavé Parisien offers three styles of the five-pound stones. Prices range from $63 to $157.

Adacia Chambers, 25, is charged with four counts of second-degree murder. She is accused of driving under the influence and plowing her car into a crowd. The crash killed a toddler, a graduate student and a couple who'd worked at the school for decades. Dozens were injured and 4 died as a result of the crash.

Frida Ghitis: Robert De Niro made a joke about first ladies, and Newt Gingrich said it was “inexcusable and the president should apologize for him” Ghitis asks: When did we get it in our heads that we have the right to never hear anything we don’t like? She says Maher has a point about the way political parties exploit their opponents’ impolite or, sometimes, merely impolitic comments. Ghitis says Maher and Rush Limbaugh have a constitutional right to express themselves.

A federal court approved a $25 million settlement on Tuesday with students who said they were duped by Donald Trump and his now-defunct Trump University. The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco finalized the settlement after it was first approved by a judge last March following an appeal by Sherri Simpson. Simpson had wanted to opt out of a class action suit in order to pursue a separate suit against Trump, but the court rejected that.

“There are no excuses. The governor long ago knew about the lead in Flint’s water. He did nothing. As a result, hundreds of children were poisoned. Thousands may have been exposed to potential brain damage from lead. Gov. Snyder should resign,” Sanders said.

We have taken data available in Wikidata and DBpedia on 'Military Conflicts' to create this interactive visualisation. Since battles usually have a place and a date, it would be nice to import this data into a data design in nodegoat and visualise these battles through time and space (diachronic geospatiality ftw)

Jupiter rises in the east as the sun is setting below the western horizon. Opposition marks the middle of the best time of year to see a planet. At this 2018 opposition, Jupiter shines in front of the constellation Libra the Scales. Jupiter comes to opposition about every 13 months.

30,000 Brits have signed a petition calling for Donald Trump to be banned from entering the United Kingdom. Petition is asking Theresa May to ban the would-be politician from setting foot on British soil. 'The UK has banned entry to many individuals for hate speech,’ the petition reads. ‘This same principle should apply to Donald J Trump'

Lawrence Russell Brewer was executed Wednesday for the hate crime slaying of James Byrd Jr. Brewer asked for two chicken fried steaks, a triple-meat bacon cheeseburger, fried okra, a pound of barbecue, three fajitas, a meat lover's pizza, a pint of ice cream. Prison officials said Brewer didn't eat any of it.

A group of 3,000 Swedish file sharers have succeeded in getting their organisation, called the Church of Kopimism, recognised as a religion by the Swedish authorities. The movement has been trying to gain official recognition for their beliefs in sharing and data copying since 2010. The church's name comes from "Kopimi", pronounced "copy me", the organisation believes that communication and sharing is sacred and needs to be respected.

Thrasher magazine co-founder ID’d as suicide in front of Mission Police Station. Eric Swenson shot himself around 8:30 a.m. without going inside the police station or talking to any officers. Loved ones believe the longtime San Franciscan's struggle with a debilitating motorcycle injury led to the suicide.

China says its military in contact with U.S. on "appropriately handling" drone seizure. The drone was being operated by civilian contractors to conduct oceanic research. It was seized while collecting unclassified scientific data in the South China Sea. The incident is likely to fray the already tense relations between U.N. and China.

Twitter, Facebook and chatrooms in instant messaging apps are buzzing with speculation about whether Trump would follow through on campaign rhetoric. News of Trump's widening lead hit hard in Cuba, which has spent the last two years negotiating normalization with the United States. A couple of Chinese participants at a U.S. Embassy event in Beijing say they'd welcome a Trump presidency.

A judge sets bail at $1.5 million for Officer Jason Van Dyke. The veteran officer posts $150,000 bond, the 10 percent of the bail amount. The mayor’s office announces plans to create a “Task Force on Police Accountability’

An off-duty California Highway Patrol officer returned $120,000 to its rightful owner. The sergeant had to swerve to avoid two large bank deposit bags in the road. She took a U-turn to pick them up and found a large amount of cash. Police were able to track down the owner and return the money to him.

The National Hurricane Center says the threat in coming days is sustained rains that could unleash "catastrophic" flooding. The city of Victoria, about 60 miles (96 kilometers) north of Rockport, had received more than 16 inches of rain by Saturday morning. Rockport Mayor Charles "C.J." Wax says some homes and businesses were heavily damaged or even completely destroyed.

Archaeologists will this week test if the Bayeux Tapestry correctly depicts Harold II’s death, when they scan a graveyard to investigate whether he in fact survived the Battle of Hastings. History books currently record he was wounded in the eye by a Norman arrow and then hacked down by four Norman knights at a turning point of British history on October 14, 1066. But an amateur historian believes Harold Godwinson may have survived and lived for another 40 years as a hermit.

Kim Kardashian robbed at gunpoint by men disguised as police in Paris. Five armed men stole a jewellery box containing valuables worth €6m (£5.2m) They also made off with a ring worth €4m, and mobile telephones. Spokeswoman for the reality TV star said she was “badly shaken but physically unharmed’ Kardashian West had been in Paris since last week for fashion week.

Lawyer: Tamerlan and Dzhokhar Tsarnaev befriended anti-U.S. government conspiracy theorist. Donald Larking, 67, was shot in the head in 1974 in an attempted robbery while working in a convenience store. Attorney: The brothers "were very helpful, very kind" to the couple. Authorities say the Tsarnaev brothers orchestrated the marathon bombing.

Brian Howard, 36, of Naperville has been charged with one felony count of Destruction of Aircraft or Aircraft Facilities. He allegedly set a fire in the basement of an Aurora FAA facility, cut the feeds to the radar and damaged the communications system. Howard remains hospitalized with self-inflicted stab wounds and is under police guard.

Chicago-based United Airlines updated its boarding process to rely on fewer boarding lanes. The move will cut down on congestion and potentially speed up passenger loading. United is also launching push notifications for those who have the airline's mobile app. Top tier or "1K" elite members will be able to pre-board before the official process.

62 percent of voters said 'Yes', making Ireland the first country to adopt same-sex marriage via a popular vote. The Catholic Church, which teaches that homosexual activity is a sin, saw its dominance of Irish politics collapse after a series of child sex abuse scandals in the early 1990s. The proposal was backed by all political parties, championed by big employers and endorsed by celebrities.

California fish market owner buys 70-pound octopus just to set it free. Octopuses, some 300 species of which inhabit waters around the world, can change colors, squirt out poison and exert a force greater than their own. In fact, the animals are part of an elite group of slimy mollusks known as cephalopods.

House Republicans have moved to impeach IRS Commissioner John Koskinen. The move comes days after the Justice Department concluded its investigation into IRS targeting of Tea Party groups with no charges filed. Rep. Elijah Cummings, ranking member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, compared GOP efforts to the Benghazi and Planned Parenthood investigations.

Port St. Lucie police officers nabbed the 12-foot, 120-pound Burmese python Friday after responding to reports of an extremely large snake on a block with homes. Police said the python killed one neighborhood cat and may be responsible for the recent disappearance of several others. The captured python belonged to an owner who had a license to keep it.

Dr. Kamran Ahmed said he wasn't the only one Dr. Henry Bello had a problem with. Bello arrived at Bronx Lebanon Hospital in the Bronx on Friday with an assault rifle. He asked for a doctor he blamed for his having to resign, but the doctor wasn't there at the time. Authorities said Bello went to the 16th and 17th floors and started shooting.

Warren Weinstein was abducted from his home in Lahore, Pakistan, on August 13. Al Qaeda chief Ayman al-Zawahiri announced in a recording that the terror outfit is holding hostage an American development worker. Weinstein headed up the Pakistan office for consulting firm J.E. Austin Associates, Inc.

Rainier Beach United Methodist Church no longer authorized to be charter partner. Boy Scout troops must have a charter partner, which often offers a place to meet and financial support. The scouting organization bans gay adults from membership. An openly gay man, Geoff McGrath, runs the troop at Rainier Beach.

An eyewitness says he joined about a dozen Secret Service agents and a few U.S. military specialists at a strip club in San Salvador a few days before President Obama and his family arrived in El Salvador to meet with its new president, Mauricio Funes. This source witnessed the majority of the men drink heavily ("wasted," "heavily intoxicated") at the strip club. The story is largely similar to the events that led up to an incident in Colombia earlier this month that prompted a widespread investigation into the agency.

Michael T. Flynn’s rise and fall followed familiar patterns in Washington, where ambitious figures secure positions of great authority only to lose them. But rarely has an official at such a high level risen and fallen in such a dizzyingly short time, in this case just 24 days after Mr. Flynn arrived in the West Wing. Rush Limbaugh said the media helped force Michael Flynn out of his post.

A police helicopter fired on Venezuela's Supreme Court and Interior Ministry in what President Nicolas Maduro said was a thwarted "terrorist attack" The confusing exchange, which is bound to ratchet up tensions in a country already paralyzed by months of deadly anti-government protests, took place as Maduro was speaking live on state television Tuesday. "We have two choices: to be judged tomorrow by our consciousness and the people, or to free the people from this corrupt government," the man said while reading from a statement.

Domnica Cemortan says she was in a romantic relationship with the captain. She was on the Costa Concordia bridge when it ran aground in January 2012. Captain Francesco Schettino faces multiple charges of manslaughter. 32 people died in the disaster off the north-west Italian coast.

Nick Stoeberl showcases all 10.1cm of his amazing tongue to snap up his tongue-tastic record. Nick’s father was “a huge fan of KISS” and as a child Nick would imitate Gene Simmons’ infamous tongue pose, realising for the first time that his tongue was longer than others. The 18-year-old from Michigan believes she has the world's longest TONGUE measuring a whopping 4 inches.

Roseanne is returning to ABC. The network has handed out an eight-episode straight-to-series order for a revival. The reboot will feature returning stars Roseanne Barr and John Goodman. Roseanne centered on the working-class Conner family in Illinois and ran from 1988-97.

Donald Trump wants to build a wall on the Mexico-US border. On Sunday's Last Week Tonight, John Oliver took Trump's policy proposal seriously. There are lots of problems, according to Oliver: Cost, geography, and effectiveness. Ultimately, Oliver suggested that buying a $75 electric waffle iron for every American would be a better use of the money.

Cobb County police Lt. Greg Abbott was recorded on video saying "we only shoot black people" Chief Mike Register: "There's really no place for these types of comments in law enforcement" Abbott, who had been an officer for 28 years, was placed on administrative leave while the department investigated.

Witnesses reported seeing a blue glow emanating from the object that raced over the east Mediterranean island's Troodos mountain range shortly before midnight Thursday. There were no reports of casualties or damage from the phenomenon. Meteors are pieces of comet or asteroid from outer space that create a fireball as they hit the Earth's atmosphere.

Four Japanese tourists complain of being overcharged in Venice. Four steaks, a fried fish platter and mineral water, according to early reports. Italian media did not name the restaurant, but said it was owned by a Chinese woman. Venice police have opened a probe after a complaint from the 25 Aprile association.

Experts from the UN's cultural body Unesco have examined a wreck off the coast of Haiti. US marine archaeologist Barry Clifford said in May that he believed he had found the wreck of Columbus's flagship. The ship, the Santa Maria, ran aground near Haiti in December 1492. But the artefacts found at the site "were those of a more recent ship", experts say.

Luxury jeweller Tiffany blames 'recent election-related activity' at Trump Tower for hitting sales at its flagship store. Many of the demonstrations before and after the election have centred on the president-elect’s skyscraper. Tiffany said worldwide net sales rose by 1% to $949m (£761m) and comparable store sales fell by 2% over the period.

Report: Some U.S. weapons bought in 2015 ended up in hands of ISIS within two months. Weapons found on front lines include machine guns laced with amphetamines, drones modified in terrorist factories and a rifle made in Nazi Germany. The findings are based on three years of meticulous documentation of weapons recovered from ISIS on battlefields of Iraq and Syria.

John McCone replaced Allen Dulles as director of central intelligence in November 1961. After JFK’s assassination in Dallas in November 1963, President Lyndon Johnson kept McCone in place at the CIA. The CIA director became an important witness before the Warren Commission. The most important information McCone withheld from the commission in its 1964 investigation was the existence of CIA plots to assassinate Castro.

Rosie O'Donnell suffered a major heart attack last week but kept it a secret. She revealed the whole scary ordeal on her blog ... as a poem. She experienced chest pains, clammy skin, and vomiting ... she then took an aspirin. The next day she went to see a cardiologist and was informed by her doctor.

Neal McDonough gave up his part on the new ABC show Scoundrels just three days into filming. The script called for him to be in a sex scene with sultry actress Virginia Madsen. The married Catholic father-of-three has made clear he won't do sex scenes.

Nomura Holdings Inc. and Royal Bank of Scotland Group Plc may face $500 million in damages. A judge called an “enormous” deception in the sale of defective mortgage-backed securities. The ruling may spur other banks to settle similar claims tied to 2008 financial crisis.

Leslie Allen Merritt Jr. reduced his bond to zero and said he can return to his home under electronic monitoring. The reduction of the bond — once $1 million — was a major victory for defense lawyers. Defense lawyers contend that ballistic tests cast doubt on the claim by authorities. The shootings caused panic on Phoenix-area freeways.

Rebels have opened his prisons in Tripoli, freeing thousands. But only about 10,000 prisoners have been accounted for, rebel leaders say. Families and friends fear that thousands are in underground prisons or, perhaps, in mass graves. Rebel leaders based here estimate that nearly 60,000 more Libyans had disappeared.

Col Gaddafi says he is loved by all his people and denies there have been protests. He says he feels betrayed by the world leaders who have urged him to quit. US ambassador to the UN Susan Rice says interview shows he is "unfit to lead" U.S. Treasury blocks $30bn (£18.5bn) in Libyan assets.

Pentagon has made contingency plans to send small teams of special operations troops into Syria. Obama warned this week that any effort by Assad to move or use his arsenal of chemical munitions would cross a "red line" U.S. intelligence agencies believe Syria has over the years produced or acquired hundreds of tons of sarin nerve agent.

The 49-year-old star's evening started off normal enough, with Moore hosting a birthday dinner party for a friend. A source says Moore was "pretty hyper" for most of the night and was not her normal self. The actress apparently left the party several times, only to come back minutes later. Moore will be seeking treatment for anorexia and her substance abuse addictions.

Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, and JPMorgan Chase will launch an independent operation. The goal is to cut health-care costs and improve services for their U.S. employees. Details of the new company were sketchy, with principals of Amazon, Berkshire and J.P. Morgan noting that the way it will work remains to be seen.

Frank Taaffe was George Zimmerman's most visible and outspoken defender. Taaffe has a lengthy criminal record that includes charges of domestic violence and burglary. He also has a history of airing virulently racist views. “This trial is waking up white America, man,” Taaffe told The White Voice.

Yulia Skripal, 33, said to be improving rapidly after being poisoned. Salisbury NHS foundation trust said she was no longer in a critical condition. Doctors described her medical state as stable while her father remains critical. Scotland Yard said police had placed a cordon around a children’s play area.

San Juan County, Utah, declares a state of emergency in response to the closure of National Park areas. County commissioners plan to storm National Park Service barricades, take control of some parks, and reopen them to the public. "This is civil disobedience," says Phil Lyman, a CPA and county commissioner.

William McCormack, 43, says he had an appendectomy in the Adirondacks last month. McCormack is seeking unspecified damages from Lawrence Hospital and Dr. Michael Kerin, the Tuckahoe surgeon who said he removed McCormack's appendix on Jan. 27, 2013. Lawsuit claims what was actually removed from McCormack was a "yellowish mass," not his appendix.

Actor George Takei took to his Facebook page Thursday night to explain what he meant by calling Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas a “clown in blackface” He said the term was “theater lingo” that “is not racist.” “Blackface’ is a lesser known theatrical term for a white actor who blackens his face to play a black buffoon. It is instead part of a racist history in this country.

Lawsuit accuses Dr. Howard Schneider of assault, battery, false imprisonment and intentionally inflicting "severe emotional distress" Florida also is investigating the Jacksonville, Fla., pediatric dentist. The plaintiffs are seeking damages exceeding $15,000 and a jury trial. Schneider, 78, has been practicing in Jacksonville for more than 40 years.

The 33-year-old DJ was pulled over near Baker, Calif. at 10:30 am for speeding and after she refused to submit to a breathalyzer test on the scene, she was arrested. Ronson was traveling back from Las Vegas where she spun at the Lavo nightclub in the Palazzo Sunday night. The District Attorney’s office tells us it will be a day or two until it decides whether to file charges against her.

Jim Morrison was born Dec. 8, 1943, at the former Brevard Hospital on U.S. 1. His parents, Steve and Clara, moved to town when Steve was transferred to Naval Air Station Melbourne for flight training during World War II. A modest Morrison display features posters, two record albums by The Doors.

Kimberly Pappas, 25, of Wyandotte was bound over on several charges stemming from the incidents that took place March 31 at CEVA Logistics, 24450 Glendale in Redford. She was charged earlier this spring in the death of her child, which she delivered in the bathroom of the business that morning. The baby was later found in a plastic bag inside another bag at her desk. The Wayne County Medical Examiner’s Office determined the death was caused by asphyxiation.

Jared Kushner says he "did not collude with Russia nor do I know of anyone else in the campaign who did so" House Speaker Paul Ryan says special counsel Robert Mueller isn't a biased partisan. President Donald Trump calls top Democrat on the House intelligence panel "sleazy" for conducting what he says is a "biased" Russia investigation.

Hugh Grant and Sarah Jessica Parker play the Morgans, a Manhattan power couple on the outs and the brink of divorce. Grant's character is confronted by a grizzly and by a rodeo; Parker's character learns she's a dead-eye with a rifle. The Morgans' pathetic dependency on their BlackBerrys would have to be funny.

Andrew McCabe oversaw a federal criminal investigation into whether Attorney General Jeff Sessions lacked candor when testifying before Congress about contacts with Russian operatives, sources told ABC News. Democratic lawmakers have repeatedly accused Sessions of misleading them in congressional testimony and called on federal authorities to investigate. Sessions was not aware of the investigation when he decided to fire McCabe last Friday less than 48 hours before McCabe was due to retire from government.

Starting in 1996, Alexa Internet has been donating their crawl data to the Internet Archive. Flowing in every day, these data are added to the Wayback Machine after an embargo period. Great white shark tagged by cruising the East Coast of the U.S. Track me here.

Sanders supporters unable to influence the committee to adopt strong language opposing the 12-nation Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) trade pact. “We did everything we could to win that vote,” said Sanders policy adviser Warren Gunnels. On the same day, the Clinton campaign announced changes to its healthcare policy proposal, including increasing mandatory healthcare funding.

Tropical Storm Isaac cancels the first day of the Republican National Convention. Donald Trump was scheduled to deliver a "big surprise" at the convention. The real estate mogul continued his birther crusade at a reception dinner. The convention is now set to begin on Tuesday.

Marden Henge is a giant ditch and bank enclosure so buried in rich Wiltshire farmland that it has almost vanished from view. The rectangular building will welcome visitors next weekend for an open day which is part of the national festival of archaeology. The house is believed to be one of the best preserved from the period ever found in the UK.

Authorities are refusing to identify the victims who were pulled from the water. The cause of the crash is under investigation, but local pilot Bill Gardiner noted that the weather had turned stormy. The plane was en route to East Hampton Airport, when it appears to have flown directly into a thunderstorm.

Kristian Perez, 17, went missing Friday night after the Orofino High School prom. Perez was found in good health and was taken into custody without incident on a runaway charge. Perez's tuxedo jacket, one shoe and his broken cell phone were recovered in proximity to a relative’s vehicle he had ridden in.

'The Accountant' was No. 1 at the weekend box office, according to studio estimates. Kevin Hart's live comedy concert film Kevin Hart: What Now? made $11.98 million for the weekend. The Girl on the Train, starring Emily Blunt, took third place.

Accessory Outlet included a clause in its Terms of Sale that charged a $250 penalty to complaining customers. The Terms also claim the customer agrees that, even after the 90 days are up, the “sole method of dispute resolution in all cases… shall be binding arbitration to take place in New York City.”

The Internet Archive hopes that references to these archived pages will be put in place of a link that would be otherwise be broken. With about half the vote counted, the Alabama Senate race between Moore and Democrat Doug Jones is too close to call. Jones' victory is set to narrow the slim Republican majority over Democrats in the Senate to 51-49. Moore faced allegations of sexual misconduct with teenagers, dividing the GOP and Democrats.

Ryan Adams and Mandy Moore are divorcing after six years of marriage. Adams' 2014 self-titled album was one of the more downcast, melancholic LPs in the singer-songwriter's vast catalog. Patrick Dempsey and his wife of 15 years, Jillian Fink, are calling it quits.

Pete Davidson proposed to Maggie Rogers on 'SNL' promo, and Ariana Grande is not laughing. Grande, however, didn't find the joke at the expense of their split the least bit funny. The couple met on "Saturday Night Live" and became engaged just weeks after making their relationship official on Instagram in May.

For the first time in history, the complications of preterm birth outrank all other causes as the world's number one killer of young children. Of the estimated 6.3 million deaths of children under the age of five in 2013, complications from preterm births accounted for nearly 1.1 million deaths. India (361,600), Nigeria (98,300), Pakistan (75,000), Democratic Republic of the Congo (40,600) and China (37,200) are the countries with the highest rates.

Ikea is recalling about 27 million chests and dressers. The furniture can tip over and crush children if they aren't anchored to the wall. Two children died after Ikea's Malm chests fell on them in 2014. Ikea says it knows of reports of three additional deaths since 1989.

Tila Tequila was the keynote speaker at the alt-right’s coming out conference in Washington DC. She tweeted a photo of herself giving a Nazi salute with the words: “Seig [sic] heil!” Classic Tila! We got hold of her as she was arriving at the airport to ask her a bit more.

George Talley's 1979 Corvette was stolen more than three decades ago in Detroit. Last week, the silver sports car was found in Mississippi. After hearing Talley’s story on the radio this morning, General Motors offered to pick up the Corvette and deliver it to him.

CBS News is hard at work determining who will become the next host of "Face the Nation" Major Garrett, the network's chief White House correspondent, and Norah O'Donnell, the co-anchor of CBS This Morning, are two likely candidates. Jake Tapper, the CNN host who previously substituted for George Stephanopoulos on ABC's Sunday show "This Week," is a top consideration.

The swarm of around 20,000 sparked chaos when their queen got stuck in a car boot. It took five different beekeepers, park rangers and passers-by to coax them off into a cardboard box. The car’s owner returned and drove away with the queen unknowingly trapped in the back, resulting in the swarm taking up the chase. The queen was even spotted on the car's boot the next day.

Oscar-winning actor Tom Hanks gifted the White House press corps a new espresso machine. Hanks first purchased a machine for the press during the Bush administration, when he toured the break room and noticed there was no coffee maker. The “Saving Private Ryan” actor replaced that machine in March 2010 after noticing the machine looked run down.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported a $4.4 billion trading loss in its chief investment office. The company restated first-quarter earnings, reducing net income by $459 million. JPMorgan also used securities gains and an $800 million accounting benefit to help boost profit. The trading loss may complicate efforts by Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon.

Al Sharpton, Whoopi Goldberg, Sienna Miller and Bryan Cranston have all threatened to leave the U.S. if Donald Trump is elected. Bill O'Reilly said he would move to Ireland if Bernie Sanders is elected president. Donald Trump's sons Eric and Donald Jr. responded to the remarks on Fox and Friends.

Lindsay Lohan had a constant stream of regular visitors while in rehab at Cliffside Malibu. RadarOnline.com has exclusively learned one unexpected visitor was actor and producer, Ben Affleck. Howard Stern spoke with Rolling Stone writer Neil Strauss for over three hours. Stern discussed his divorce from his ex-wife Alison, the wild period in his personal life that followed before he met his second wife Beth. Stern also spoke about former sidekick Artie Lange's suicide attempt, his many years in therapy.

A group of 18 House Republicans has formally nominated President Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize. The lawmakers tapped Trump for his efforts to denuclearize the Korean Peninsula and end the 68-year-old war between North and South Korea. North Korea has agreed to cease its tests of nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles ahead of the meeting.

"Eat Pray Love" is a heavily idealized journey of self-discovery with a pretty woman. The film never ventures, even once, into a situation that does not reek of comfy familiarity. The Elizabeth Gilbert memoir on which the movie is based also got criticized for its Western fetishization of Eastern thought.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer says he questions the timing of James Comey's firing. He also questions why Attorney General Jeff Sessions "played a role in firing the man leading it" Schumer is now demanding the appointment of a special prosecutor to take over the Russia investigation. White House officials appeared to have badly misjudged the impact of Trump's sudden move.

The U.S. Army is developing a high-tech suit of armor that will make you nearly invincible. The Tactical Assault Light Operator Suit, or TALOS, promises "superhuman strength" The suit has integrated 360-degree cameras not unlike Google Glass. It also has sensors that can detect injuries and apply wound-sealing foam.

Unearthed grave sheds light on Batavia shipwreck mass murder. A new grave has been discovered almost four centuries after the Batavia was wrecked on Morning Reef, within the Abrolhos Islands. The Dutch East India vessel was on its maiden voyage when it wrecked with more than 300 people on board. The survivors managed to swim to the nearby Beacon Island, but about 40 people drowned.

An anonymous benefactor has donated $34 million for education, jobs, health care, housing and technology skills. The gift will help build 731 affordable housing units, create about 2,500 jobs and channel millions for early-childhood education and African-American student achievement. "It was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity," said Fred Blackwell, CEO of the San Francisco Foundation.

The Animas River was closed to tubers, rafters and kayakers Thursday as the toxic plume made its way through Durango. The closure went into effect at 3 p.m., and it will remain in effect indefinitely until the river is deemed safe. The city of Durango stopped pumping water out of the Animas river on Wednesday to prevent contaminating the city reservoir.

Ryan Lock, 20, from Chichester, West Sussex, died on 21 December. He was fighting as a volunteer with the Kurdish armed fighting forces, the YPG. Mr Lock, a chef, had travelled to Syria in August having told friends and family he was going on holiday to Turkey.

Sahray Astina Barber, 22, was last seen around 6 a.m. Monday as she made her way to work. Barber has been living at a 212-unit apartment complex on Northpark Boulevard, across the street from the campus of Cal State San Bernardino. Police are trying to determine if the attacks and disappearance are related.

The supporting cast was strong: Laura Benanti was appropriately sultry as Elsa Von Hottie, while Christian Borle was appropriately hammy as Max Detweiler.

With Charity for All: Why Charities Are Failing and a Better Way to Give is Ken Stern's new book. Stern argues that most of the nonprofit sector is financially inept at best, and downright unsavory at worst. Investigating the financials of charities can be time-consuming, frustrating, and near impossible.

Two former bodyguards of Gisele Bundchen and Tom Brady jailed for five years. The shooting took place in April 2009 as the couple celebrated their wedding. A third man - Manuel Valverde - was acquitted of the charges. The court also ordered the defendants to pay five million colones ($10,000)

The Dow, which had been up about 130 points, fell into the red within two minutes, and then bounced back just as quickly as it became obvious that the "news" was false, and a prank. The Syrian Electronic Army claimed responsibility for the attack.

Glenna Duram, 46, found guilty of first-degree murder and a felony firearm charge. Martin Duram was shot five times and found dead in their Ensley Township home in May 2015. Family members said the couple’s pet, an African grey parrot named Bud, seemed to replay the murder.

Recall organizers file a notice of intent to recall Judge Aaron Persky. They also submit a statement branding the judge as an apologist for rapists and batterers. Persky gave a lenient sentence to former Stanford athlete Brock Turner for sexually assaulting an unconscious, intoxicated woman. The judge has seven days to submit his up to 198-word response.

Frida Ghitis: President Obama claims energy open-mindedness, but his policy is “all of the above.” She says he opposes drilling off the Mid-Atlantic coast, Florida Gulf Coast, Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. First example of fossilised brain tissue from a dinosaur. Fossil, most likely from a species closely related to Iguanodon, displays distinct similarities to the brains of modern-day crocodiles and birds. Meninges - the tough tissues surrounding the actual brain - as well as tiny capillaries and adjacent cortical tissues have been preserved as mineralised 'ghosts'

The parent company of Joe's Crab Shack is testing a no-tipping policy at 18 of its 131 locations. The test by Houston-based Ignite Restaurant Group scraps tips in exchange for raising wages for its restaurant workers. Joe’s test comes a month after famed New York restaurateur Danny Meyer announced plans to eliminate tipping at all of his restaurants.

Susan Carland, wife of The Project host Waleed Aly, has found a way to channel the daily abuse she receives at the hands of Twitter trolls. The respected Muslim sociologist is donating $1 for every hateful tweet she receives. Carland has already donated over $1000 to the worthy cause.

Police have a 12-year-old suspect in custody: Mason Campbell, a seventh-grader at the school. Campbell, who smuggled a 20-gauge shotgun with the wood stock sawed off into the school, warned several students not to attend school today, police say. Campbell was transferred to a psychiatric hospital in Albuquerque.

Records show two heart transplant patients stayed in the same room where mold was found. One of the patients had lichtheimia and died in October 2014; the other had rhizomucor. The hospital shut down the cardiothoracic ICU for cleaning and analysis.

Manipulator modificaputis is thought to have lived 100 million years ago. It has a triangular, manoeuvrable head, with large eyes, set upon a long neck. It also had a narrow body and wings, elongated legs and mouthparts. Discovery adds to the number of ferocious cockroaches known.

Auto makers aim to make 2014 the year that cars connect to the Web in a big way. Some of the world's biggest automakers are working with Google to bring its Android software into vehicle infotainment systems. The announcement comes the day before the official opening of the International Consumer Electronics Show.

Roy Oliver turned himself in Friday night, just hours after the Dallas County Sheriff's Office issued a warrant for his arrest in the April 29 death of 15-year-old Jordan Edwards. Oliver fired a rifle at a car full of teenagers leaving a party, fatally shooting Edwards. The teen's death led to protests calling for Oliver to be fired and charged.

The one-bedroom, two-bathroom custom house has the interior ambience of a bright cave. Free-form walls punctuated with expanses of glass bring in ocean views. Clark, 82, hosted "American Bandstand" for more than three decades starting in the '50s.

Jeff Herman is one of America’s most high-profile and controversial lawyers of the moment. He is suing “X-Men” director Bryan Singer and three other Hollywood power-players for the alleged sexual assault of two clients. The defendants strenuously deny the allegations, and say Herman is a publicity-courting grandstander.

John Avlon: Obama's debt-ceiling speech was condescending to citizens. He says Obama's $2.4 trillion increase does precisely what Obama says it doesn't: it "allow[s] Congress to spend more money" Avlon says House Speaker John Boehner's performance was a display of mendacity.
