A total lunar eclipse of a "blue moon" will occur on Jan. 31, 2018. The online, free lunar total eclipse session is scheduled for 11:30 UT. Later the same day, we will show the Supermoon rising above Rome. The eclipse will take place during the middle of the night, and the Pacific Ocean will be turned toward the moon at the time.

Margaret Gieszinger, 52, of Exeter, was arrested on suspicion of corporal injury to a child. Students say they don't know what triggered her behavior but say she had a similar breakdown earlier this week. Police interviewed students and watched cell phone footage of the incident.

Florida’s coral reefs are experiencing a multi-year outbreak of coral disease. The disease outbreak is highly prevalent and is estimated to have resulted in the mortality of millions of corals. The exact cause and contributing factors for this event will likely take years to identify. addressing other known coral stressors will increase the ability of the corals to recover.

Yahoo! Inc. agreed to sell its main web businesses to Verizon Communications Inc. for $4.8 billion. The all-cash deal includes Yahoo real estate, but excludes some intellectual property. Yahoo will be left with its stakes in Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and Yahoo Japan Corp., with a combined market value of about $40 billion.

Doug Ford's Progressive Conservatives have won the provincial election in Canada's most populous province. Ford is the brother of late Toronto Mayor Rob Ford, who became famous for smoking crack cocaine. Doug Ford is a populist who has been compared to U.S. President Donald Trump. A Liberal defeat Thursday was predicted by outgoing Liberal Premier Kathleen Wynne herself.

Rachel Uchitel was married in 2004 but it only lasted a year and 4 months. Matt was a football player at Penn State and is now a businessman in San Francisco. The two have been living together in San Fran for several months. "Expecting big things for 2012... Five down, Four months to go," she tweeted Tuesday.

JBS Tolleson, Inc. is recalling approximately 6,937,195 pounds of various raw, non-intact beef products that may be contaminated with Salmonella Newport. The products were packaged on various dates from July 26, 2018 to Sept. 7, 2018. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them.

A version of Edvard Munch’s “The Scream,” one of the most recognizable images in art history, sold at Sotheby's on Wednesday night for just under $120 million. Five bidders competed for the work, which sold to a telephone bidder. The previous record for an artwork sold at auction was $106.5 million for Picasso's "Nude, Green Leaves, and Bust"

NEW: The strike is likely to raise tensions in a standoff with Washington over NATO supply routes to Afghanistan. OSCE holding special meeting in Vienna to discuss developments in Ukraine. Obama administration accused Russia on Wednesday of orchestrating a new military...

Bavaria's police say their colleagues in Bergen found a gate with the Nazi slogan "Arbeit Macht Frei" ("Work sets you free") After receiving photos from Norway, the police say it is "highly likely" to be the infamous gate. Police got an anonymous tip that led to the find and a source said no arrests had been made.

Alarms went off when the would-be thief tried to break through the glass box. The suspect was held on suspicion of attempted theft of the document. It is claimed to be the best preserved of four original Magna Cartas. The man was wrestled to the ground by staff when he attempted to flee after the attempted raid at 16:45 BST.

Minnie Driver has been working steadily in film and television since 1998. Her latest film, Hunky Dory, is a sweet if slightly odd high-school musical set in Wales during the heatwave of 1976. She hasn't made a Hollywood blockbuster since Hard Rain – the 1998 disaster thriller that seemed to kick off a barrage of negative press.

The Drudge Report has portrayed Ted Cruz's win in Colorado as a corrupt power grab. The site named for Matt Drudge, who broke the story of Bill Clinton’s affair with Monica Lewinsky and still runs it, links to nine stories this morning with salacious headlines about the convention.

Jessica Dutro, 25, is charged with murder, murder by abuse and second-degree assault. Her 4-year-old son, Zachary, died from injuries related to a beating in August 2012. Her boyfriend, Brian Canady, pleaded guilty earlier this month to first-degree manslaughter.

"The Other Guys" is a new goofballs-and-fireballs comedy directed by Adam McKay. Will Ferrell uses his big body, his quick mind and his infinitely fungible voice to yoke disparate and ridiculous traits into a brand new and yet instantly archetypal comic character. The plot is neither the movie's point nor its most memorable feature.

An Egyptian court has reportedly jailed Shaimaa Ahmed, a singer who was arrested last month for a provocative music video. Ahmed, 25, who goes by the name Shyma professionally, was found guilty of inciting debauchery and publishing an indecent film. Her music video featured the singer suggestively eating a banana. The director of the music video for Ahmed's song, "I Have Issues," was also sentenced to two years in prison.

Sixty-one-year-old Leslie Kahn was swimming in her pool Aug. 11 when the ladder broke. She used a pool pole to drag the chair her iPad was on and posted in a community Facebook page, asking for help. A woman who lived nearby showed up, followed by police and a neighbor.

Citigroup Inc. will seek approval for a “meaningful” payout to shareholders after failing to meet minimum standards in U.S. stress tests. SunTrust Banks Inc., Ally Financial Inc. and MetLife Inc. also fell short in the Fed’s test. Citigroup fell 3.2 percent to $35.27 at 11:50 a.m. in New York, the biggest drop on the 24-company KBW Bank Index.

Newark Mayor Cory Booker won Tuesday's Democratic primary for the U.S. Senate. Booker's opponent will be Republican Steven Lonegan, a former mayor of Bogota, N.J. The liberal critique of Booker is that he's too chummy with Wall Street bankers and Silicon Valley moguls.

Seattle Seahawks cornerback Jeremy Lane has already joined the protest, and now linebacker Bobby Wagner and receiver Doug Baldwin may join him. Baldwin said he has heard from veterans who have supported a series of tweets he posted defending the protest. Wagner said he couldn't say exactly what the team might do, saying "whatever we decide to do will be a big surprise"

The retired King of the Belgians has been ordered to take a DNA paternity test by a Brussels court. It raises the prospect of finally resolving whether he is the real father of Delphine Boël, a 50-year-old aristocrat artist. King Albert II must submit to the test within three months or be legally presumed to be her father.

Democratic Sen. Jon Tester says it's time for Congress to tackle the nation's pressing problems. Tester, 56, led by 16,000 votes over U.S. Rep. Denny Rehberg late Wednesday. The contest was the most expensive in Montana history, as both candidates spent $20 million.

Pro-independence party candidate Tsai Ing-wen took a commanding lead in Taiwan's presidential election results late Saturday evening. The candidate for the China-friendly Nationalist Party conceded a massive loss. Tsai had about 60 percent of votes while Nationalist Eric Chu had about 30 percent, with about half of votes counted.

Driver of Spanish train that derailed, killing at least 80 people, is under police guard in hospital. Eight-carriage train came off tracks, hit a wall and caught fire just outside Santiago de Compostela. Authorities canceled festivities as the city went into mourning. One local official described the aftermath of the crash as like a scene from hell.

Christian Barnes, 22, was arrested for investigation of possessing a destructive device. No one was injured in the small blast, but Disneyland briefly evacuated the Mickey's Toontown section. Detectives found fragments of a water bottle in the trash can and believe Barnes placed dry ice inside it. Police described Barnes as a vendor who peddled sodas on a mobile cart.

Video shot inside the Beta Theta Pi house was being shown from the night the pledge was ordered to drink.

No ticket matched all six numbers for the $458 million jackpot, pushing the estimated prize for the next drawing to $502 million. It's the fourth time in the game's history that the jackpot has surged past half a billion dollars.

Deborah Skouson of St. George needed to find a shirt for her 10-year-old daughter. Her daughter Cami, who has autism, loves to wear a pink flowered top from Target. The request quickly went viral with over 22,000 shares overall.

Madsen, 47, is charged with murder, dismemberment and indecent handling of a corpse over the death of Ms. Wall. He has denied murder and said Wall died accidentally inside the submarine, but has confessed to cutting up her body and throwing the body parts into the sea.

A 51-year-old woman died at Northwestern Memorial Hospital. Eight others, including the bus driver, were hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. The Route 148 Clarendon/Michigan Express bus was eastbound on Lake Street just before 6 p.m. The accordion-style bus had been headed east on Lake and stopped at a red light at Michigan Avenue.

Two people and two dogs are traveling the country, coexisting in 98 square feet of living space. It’s their version of the tiny house movement, downsizing and taking a do-it-yourself approach to home ownership. “We don’t really have enough time to do a true yard sale so this is our, like, piecemeal please-everybody-come-take-our-stuff,” Kelly Tousley says.

Some 265 people have died and 1,140 have been injured in the 7.2 magnitude quake. Nearly 1,000 buildings have been destroyed in the disaster zone, with the town of Ercis the worst hit. The death toll is expected to rise as outlying areas are reached. Some 2,400 rescue workers are involved in the relief effort.

"Live Funny or Die" launched Nov. 8, with an introductory video featuring most of the Republican candidates. Mitt Romney, Ron Paul, Michele Bachman and Rick Perry are all represented. President Obama impersonator Reggie Brown also makes a cameo at the end to explain the only two things you need to hold a captive audience.

Brock Turner, 20, was sentenced last week to six months in jail and three years' probation for sexually assaulting an unconscious woman. Turner blamed his actions on Stanford's "party culture" while simultaneously turning himself into the victim of his own horrific actions. Turner will remain in protective custody, as perpetrators of sexual assault are often targeted by other inmates.

Warner Bros. plans to produce 10 DC Comics movies between 2016 to 2020. The company is so focused on dethroning Marvel as the reigning box office champ. The great asset of Marvels movies like “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Iron Man’ and “Captain America” is their sense of humor.

Netflix is teaming up with Leonardo DiCaprio to release the documentary Virunga. The film centers on park rangers and the gorillas they protect. The doc will be release simultaneously on Netflix and in theaters in New York and Los Angeles on Nov. 7.

Michael Lohan has popped the question to Jon Gosselin's ex, Kate Major. Lohan says he was waiting for the "situation with Lindsay to resolve" He has been encouraging his troubled daughter to enter rehab. Major tells Us, "The ring is gorgeous!"

Secretary of State John Kerry said on Sunday it's now "pretty clear" that separatists were responsible for the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 in Ukraine. Kerry said he knows "for certain" that within the last month a convoy of armored personnel carriers, rocket launchers, tanks and artillery crossed over the Russian border into Eastern Ukraine and was turned over to separatists.

WFP’s executive director David Beasley said in an emailed statement to the Guardian later on Tuesday that the agency would republish the report.

Jonathan Tieu, 20, Bac Duong, 43, and Hossein Nayeri, 37, were all awaiting trial for various violent crimes before they escaped the jail on Friday. "There's speculation, but there's nothing," Sen. Dianne Feinstein says. "I'm not going to go in to what we do have or what we don't have," she says. Russia's ambassador to the U.S. says Russia won't leave Crimea because it's now Russian territory.

Freedom Industries Inc. filed a Chapter 11 petition with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in the Southern District of West Virginia. Company president Gary Southern signed the paperwork, which lists the company's assets and liabilities. It says the company has at least 200 creditors and owes its top 20 creditors $3.66 million.

The depth of Loch Ness changed by 1.5 millimeters (0.06 inches) at its different ends depending on whether the North Sea tide was in or not. The researchers used pressure sensors distributed throughout Loch Ness to measure depth changes to the incredible accuracy of 0.1 mm ( 0.004 in) over the 35 km (22 mi) length. The water in the loch acts like a bowl of water on a wobbly table, sloshing according to the movement of the land it rests upon.

Sources tell Fox News that Susan Rice requested to unmask the names of Trump transition officials caught up in surveillance. Names were part of incidental electronic surveillance of candidate and President-elect Trump and people close to him, including family members. White House Press Secretary Sean Spicer declined to comment specifically on what role Rice may have played or officials’ motives.

President Obama delivered his eighth and final speech as president to the U.N. General Assembly Tuesday. Obama sought to use his last appearance before the global body to define how his leadership had put the world on a better trajectory over the last eight years. The president warned that the forces of globalization have exposed "deep fault lines"

Twitch user AnaPlaying was live streaming herself playing League of Legends. She accidentally lit her hair on fire while talking to her followers. Although she seems pretty shocked by her burning hair, she doesn't look hurt. She laughs off the fact that she lit her head on fire in front of a bunch of people.

Justice Anthony Kennedy’s retirement is a good moment to step back and realize just how broken the process for selecting Supreme Court justices now is. The minority party no longer holds a scintilla of power over Supreme Court picks. The majority party can and will jam whomever they want onto the Court, where that person will serve for life. No one knows when the next seat will open.

Pedro Viloria, a worker who mans the drive-thru, jumped through the ordering window at a McDonald’s in Doral, Fla., to help a woman who suddenly became unconscious while operating her vehicle. Surveillance footage also shows Viloria pulling the off-duty officer from the SUV as it rolled forward. A second McDonald's employee, along with paramedics who were in the restaurant, helped to revive the woman.

Record levels are expected over the next three days from the surging River Danube. The river is expected to peak near the border with Slovakia, in Nagybajcs, on Saturday. Concern is growing that the surging Danube might break into a reservoir containing toxic waste. The swollen Elbe River menaces the state of Saxony-Anhalt in eastern Germany.

A Las Vegas judge on Friday threw out a case against Kirstin Blaise Lobato, who spent more than a decade behind bars for the killing of a homeless man whose penis was cut off. The Innocence Project has agreed to take her case. Lobato allegedly killed Duran Bailey in July 2001 and mutilated his body to include severing his penis.

Researchers in South Korea studied 10,711 adults, a representative sample of the Korean population enrolled in a large survey of health and nutrition. The study found that women who ate instant noodles at least twice a week were 68 percent more likely to have metabolic syndrome. The effect was not apparent in men.

Kempton A. Bonds, 19, of Clifton, Md., has been charged with second-degree murder. He is accused of stabbing Tyonne Johns, 35, during an argument over folding chairs at a wedding. Bonds called police after becoming aggravated by the behavior of the wedding guests.

Facebook will start using face recognition technology to assist its users in tagging pictures. Users will still get a notice if they are tagged and can remove the tag of any photos. Facebook will roll out the service to a small number of users next week and expand from there. It will initially only be available in the United States.

“Sausage Party” scored at the box office this weekend, debuting to a meaty $33.6 million. “Suicide Squad’ topped domestic charts with $43.8 million, bringing its stateside total to a hefty $222.9 million.

If all goes well, the Curiosity rover will be on the Mars surface at about 1:17 a.m. Eastern time. If not, the waiting time for a final answer on whether the rover was safely on the surface could range from two to eight hours. The landing, which could never be tested in full on Earth, includes a hovering rocket stage, to lower it to the ground.

A law professor at the University of Alberta is calling out the school's faculty of medicine for scheduling a workshop called "Spoon Bending and the Power of the Mind" Timothy Caulfield, a professor of health law and science policy at U of A, tweeted a poster for the workshop on Wednesday. Authorities are considering false reporting charges against one person who was more prankster than tipster. Police say that Dorner has killed three people and injured others.

Sanders argued that super delegates should follow the popular vote from the states they represent, but also said they should consider backing him even if he does not win the majority of pledged delegates.

ProPublica and NPR have found the military's brain injury testing program has failed to deliver on its promise. The military chose a test that wasn't actually proven to detect TBI. More than a million troops have taken the test at a cost of more than $42 million to taxpayers.

A 73-year-old man’s spotless driving record nearly got him off the hook during a traffic stop Tuesday night. Officer Nic Abts-Olsen saw the driver portioning out a scoop of cocaine from a small glass vial. The man initially denied having any cocaine, though he admitted he had “vitamins” in his possession.

Anthony J. Lescowitch Jr., 35, of Drifton, was wanted by Freeland police for aggravated assault and other charges since Nov. 27, 2013. Police posted his picture on the department's Facebook account on Monday, hoping to track him down with community help. Multiple people shared the information on their own pages to assist police but, to the surprise of officers, so did L Escowitch. An undercover officer posing as a female on Facebook, an officer began to converse with LEscowitch about his wanted picture.

Donald Trump says the U.S. should consider racial profiling as a terrorism-fighting tool. Trump's comments come one week after 49 people were shot and killed in a gay nightclub in Orlando. The presumptive presidential nominee says other countries use profiling and "it's not the worst thing to do"

Cops: Connecticut Burglar Gets Tripped Up By Stolen Sweatshirt And Its Vigilant Owner. Derek Benson, 30, already facing multiple burglary charges has been arrested on new criminal counts. Benson was spotted wearing a stolen sweatshirt in a mug shot photo, police report.

Apple will start selling the iPhone 4S in mainland China on Jan. 13. China is one of the world's largest mobile device markets, with close to a billion cellphone users. The iPhone now accounts for nearly half of Apple's annual revenue, and some analysts believe it earns the company more than 60% of its profits.

A settler forgot where he buried $100,000 in gold around the Bay Area. Granville P. Swift was known for many things, but he was not known for his memory. The Kentuckian had come to California as a 19-year-old, nine years before Gold Rush.

YouTube has a new top-viewed video of all time. Wiz Khalifa's video for "See You Again" featuring Charlie Puth became the site's most-watched video Monday. The video is about 2 million more than the video for Korean rapper Psy's 2012 smash "Gangnam Style" Justin Bieber's "Sorry" sits in third place.

Nearly the entire class at Anderson High School was caught cheating on a final exam. A couple of students reportedly took photos of the exam answers from an answer key. School officials are also looking into disciplinary action. The entire class had to retake the final exam during summer break.

U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Chair Mary Jo White unveiled the regulator’s most sweeping plan yet for reining in high-frequency trading. Proprietary traders who use computers to buy and sell stocks in milliseconds would have to register with the SEC. Operators of dark pools, broker-owned venues that compete with exchanges and don’t publish bids and offers, would also have to provide their rules for matching buyers and sellers.

Ina Rogers says she and husband Jonathan Allen did not abuse 10 children. "Not one of my kids even has a cavity...” says Ina Rogers, defending herself and her husband against charges of abuse and torture. Fairfield police arrested Rogers' 29-year-old husband Jonathan Michael Allen on Friday after a six-week investigation.

Netflix announces unlimited maternity and paternity leave for all employees. The company suggests parents can come back to the office either part or full time, then go back out as necessary during the first year. During that first year, employees will be able to take as long as they feel they need to.

Steven Seagal has been banned from entering Ukraine for five years. Security service says he has 'committed socially dangerous actions' Actor received Russian citizenship last year and voiced support for Russia's seizure of Crimea. He has joined fellow actor Gérard Depardieu on a blacklist of cultural figures.

The surface area of a catastrophic Gulf of Mexico oil spill quickly tripled in size amid growing fears among experts that the slick could become vastly more devastating than it seemed just two days ago. President Barack Obama planned a Sunday trip to the Gulf Coast to see the damage himself. The spill is more than 130 miles long and 70 miles. The environmental mess could eclipse the Exxon Valdez disaster.

A hiker died on Monday after falling from the cables near the summit of Half Dome at Yosemite National Park. The victim’s body was recovered on Tuesday. Every spring, cables are put into place along the final 400 feet to help hikers make the steep ascent to the 8,839-foot granite summit.

Rudy Giuliani said the President's lawyers have not heard back from special counsel Robert Mueller's office in nearly three weeks. "I have to figure they're planning something," Giuliani said. He suggested Mueller's team could be considering issuing a report without talking to the President, or issuing a subpoena.

Bloom Energy Server converts biofuels or natural gas (along with oxygen) to electricity. Unit the size of a parking space can produce 400Kw of electricity using less fuel than a traditional power plant would require. Company promises unit that can power a home in 10 years at a cost of $3,000.

Netflix has renewed the watercooler hit "13 Reasons Why" for a second season. The streaming service announced Sunday that it has picked up the series revolving around the suicide of a high school girl. Season 2 will pick up in the aftermath of Hannah Baker’s death and the start of the characters’ journeys toward healing and recovery.

Using the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services carrier files for a 20% random sample of beneficiaries from January 1, 2008, through December 31, 2011, we identified index emergency department visits at acute care hospitals by Medicare beneficiaries. We defined an index visit as the earliest visit at which a beneficiary had an evaluation and a management claim by an emergency medicine physician with a place-of-service designation in the emergency department. For each physician, we first calculated the proportion of all emergencyDepartment visits after which an opioid prescription was filled. We grouped physicians into quartiles of rates of opioid prescribing within each hospital and classified physicians as being in the top or bottom quartile of prescribing rates.

Amazon.com plans to open a store in the middle of New York City, according to people familiar with the plans. It would be the first brick-and-mortar outlet in its 20-year history and an experiment to provide the type of face-to-face experience found at traditional retailers. The Manhattan location would function as a "mini-warehouse" for same-day delivery.

Former South Carolina Gov. Mark Sanford (R) has been having a rough few weeks in his campaign to reclaim his old House seat. Sanford accused his opponent, Elizabeth Colbert Busch, of refusing to debate him publicly. As a last resort, he said, he'd decided to instead debate "Pelosi"

Triple suicide bombers hit a pair of mosques crowded with worshippers in the Yemeni capital, Sanaa, on Friday. The attackers targeted mosques controlled by Shiite rebels. At least 137 people were killed and 357 wounded when suicide bombers, pretending to be disabled and hiding explosives under casts, attacked the mosques.

Ram Nath Kovind, a member of India's lowest Dalit caste, was elected president. It is the first time both candidates were from the lowest tier of the country's caste system. Kovind beat opposition candidate Meira Kumar, a former parliament speaker and member of the Dalit community. The largely ceremonial post is decided by 4,800 lawmakers across the country.

A robot with a head, hands and feet boarded a flight for Germany at Los Angeles International Airport on Monday. The robot, named Athena, created a scene at the Tom Bradley International Terminal as she was pushed in a wheelchair up to the Lufthansa counter to pick up her ticket to Frankfurt. This is the first time a robot has flown as a paid passenger on a commercial jet, according to the airport.

Mass cemetery was found beneath St John's College, Cambridge. It contained around 1,300 burials, including about 400 complete skeletons. Experts made the sinister discovery that many of the skeletons did not fit their graves. This suggests that some, but not all of the graves may have been dug in advance of being needed.

Vincent van Gogh cut off his ear in 1888 after a row with Paul Gauguin. The artist then gave the ear to a prostitute in a brothel in Arles, France. But a new study of his time in Provence suggests it was inspired by the news his brother Theo, his most loyal confidant, was about to marry.

GOP wants Waters, Rangel on trial before midterm election. Republicans on the House ethics committee are calling on Democrats to schedule the public trials of charges against Reps. Charles Rangel and Maxine Waters. “The Chairwoman has repeatedly refused to set either the Rangel or Waters trial before the November election,” the Republicans wrote in a statement released Tuesday.

Scott Pruitt installed a $43,000 soundproof phone booth in his office last year. Newly released records show he placed only one call to the White House. The new documents do not show how many incoming calls Pruitt received in the soundproof booth. Pruitt testified in April that he used the booth sparingly.

Christopher Myers, 50, was bitten by a great white shark off Cape Cod on Monday. He suffered serious injuries to his lower legs and will require physical therapy to fully recover. State environmental officials said yesterday they are still investigating the attack. Myers said he wishes shark warnings had been posted.

Melvin Johnson, 39, was shot and killed Tuesday on the east side of the San Francisco Bay Area city. His 16-month-old grandson and 20-year-old son were fatally shot in August 2013. Police have made no arrests and released no motive for Johnson's killing.

Joaquin "El Chapo" Guzman was transferred to a prison in Ciudad Juarez, a source says. "Due to the proximity (to the U.S.), it makes it easier to extradite him," the official says. The exact reason for the move is unclear, but it comes one month after a lawyer said his client wanted to be extradited. Mexico's government attributed Guzman's transfer to renovations intended to improve security at Altiplano.

Lonnie David Franklin, Jr., is convicted of murdering nine women and one girl. He was dubbed "The Grim Sleeper" because of a 13-year gap between slayings. The penalty phase of his trial will begin May 11. The jury took less than two days to convict Franklin of all charges against him.

A 19-month-old girl was burned to death inside a northeast Houston apartment on Monday. Her three siblings were home alone when they started to play with the oven. Case workers from Child Protective Services filed an emergency hearing to take custody of the three children. According to CPS, there have been previous reports made concerning the mother.

The U.S. government is backing away from Arctic offshore oil and gas drilling. The Department of the Interior announced the cancellation of two potential lease sales off the Alaskan coast in the Beaufort and Chukchi seas. The Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement also denied lease extension requests from two companies, Shell and Statoil. It comes after oil giant Royal Dutch Shell last month stopped its Arctic activity citing "disappointing" tests.

Jose Ines Garcia Zarate, 45, was acquitted of murder and involuntary manslaughter charges. He was convicted of being a felon in possession of a firearm, which could bring a three-year sentence. Prosecutors had argued he intentionally shot Kate Steinle, 32, with a Sig Sauer .40-caliber handgun. But his defense attorney said the shooting was accidental.

Sumatran tigers are listed as critically endangered: Only 400 to 500 exist in the wild. There are only 65 in accredited zoos in North America. The Zoo’s female Sumatran tiger, Damai, gave birth to two cubs Monday, August 5.

George Mason economist Tyler Cowen was pepper-sprayed and placed under citizen’s arrest by an unknown white male while teaching a class on the literature of vigilante justice. Cowen refused medical treatment, and tweeted the following shortly after the attack: “ Back to work! (as usual)…”

High Street shoe chain Barratts and DVD rental chain Blockbuster go into administration. More than 3,000 UK and Irish jobs at risk. It is the third time in four years the shoe chain has been in administration. Saturday marked the last day for in-store rentals at local Blockbuster outlets.

"The Cuckoo's Calling" quickly zoomed up the charts Sunday after J.K. Rowling was identified as the writer. The book features a private investigator named Cormoran Strike, who lost a leg in Afghanistan. The author had originally been described as having served in the military, where his experiences helped shape the novel.

Mayor Rahm Emanuel won praise from some representatives of Chicago's immigrant community. Some same activists contend Emanuel should do even more to prevent police from helping federal officials deport Chicago immigrants. The mayor also caught more flak from U.S. Attorney General Jeff Sessions, who in stepping up his rhetoric said "no amount of federal taxpayer dollars will help a city that refuses to help its own residents"

Social media users called Michael Phelps' "race" against a Great White shark a "scam" Phelps chose to swim side-by-side with a simulation, instead of the real thing. Phelps and the Great White each took turns running the 100 meter race course at different times.

Rutgers dismisses five players from its football team following arrests earlier this week. Coach Kyle Flood announced the dismissals about 10 minutes before the Scarlet Knights' season opener. The alleged April 25 assault that left one Rutgers University student with a broken jaw was captured on video. Investigators confiscated cellular phones from an unknown number of team members.

Many on Twitter were quick to condemn her and the publication for allowing a sympathetic figure to write the profile.

Greece must find savings worth 11.5 billion euros for 2013 and 2014 to satisfy its creditors. Prime Minister Antonis Samaras's government last week managed to draw up a list of measures to achieve those savings. The three parties in his conservative-led administration failed to agree on them, and are due to resume talks on Monday.

A new Utah law could charge women with homicide if they miscarry. Women's rights advocates are concerned that women will be brought up on murder charges for drinking, failing to wear a seatbelt, or falling down the stairs. The bill passed Utah's state legislature last Thursday and still needs final approval by the governor.

Lohan also discusses her DUI court situation, her father Michael Lohan, her alleged drug use, her tearful confession of how she must miss her brother's graduation and more.

Pakistan's electricity system is paralyzed by $5 billion in unpaid bills. At its worst, this leaves power providers with no funds to pay for fuel, so their plants slow or shut down. As a political issue, electricity has galvanized the Pakistani public. Raja Pervez Ashraf, the last prime minister, has been identified with the power crisis.

Anthony Morales, 19, and Matthew Kafker, 18, are each being held on $50,000 bail for charges of criminal damage to property, institutional vandalism and hate crime in a place of worship. A Cook County judge raised her voice at the freshmen and denounced their alleged antics during a Saturday bonding hearing. The freshmen appeared in court wearing T-shirts and jeans, and never spoke, according to the Chicago Tribune.

Florence Heene, 71, had only a few photos and the knowledge her father was a Canadian soldier stationed in Ghent, Belgium, during the Second World War. She posted a plea for information on Facebook earlier this month. Over the weekend, descendants of a veteran from Vancouver named Herbert Louis Hellyer saw Heene's photos and contacted her. "I have the piece [of my life] that I was looking for," Heene said.

Astronauts who have gone on spacewalks consistently speak of space's peculiar odor. The odor clings to their suit, helmet, gloves and tools. "It's like something I haven't ever smelled before, but I'll never forget it," NASA astronaut Kevin Ford said.

NEW: Police identify the shooter as Snochia Moseley, 26, from Baltimore County. NEW: A source close to the investigation says the woman was a disgruntled employee. The shooting is the third high-profile shooting in the US in two days. "We are closely monitoring the horrific shooting," Gov. Larry Hogan tweets.

The complaint alleges that "the WEN products at issue contain a caustic ingredient that causes a chemical reaction and damages hair and follicles"

Gabourey Sidibe is the solo cover of Elle's 25th-anniversary October issue. The actress’s skin is noticeably lighter than usual on the cover. She also has a bad weave that Elle should be ashamed to put on a cover.

Lifetime announced Wednesday a new series titled Born in the Wild. The series chronicles pregnant women giving birth outdoors, unassisted by doctors. There's also a "Project Runway" spinoff for teens called "Threads" Also in development: shows with the self-explanatory titles "Ugly Models" and "Worst Stylist Ever"

This often leads to dominance from the larger players who have more money to spend. In China, however, where there are only two or three major state-run networks dominating the market, this model is very fitting.

Girl’s arrival on Fernando de Noronha on Saturday came as a surprise to everyone – including the parents. First baby in 12 years born on remote island where births are banned. Expectant mothers are told to travel to the mainland, where the nearest big city is Natal.

Sen. Lindsey Graham and Sen. Joe Lieberman were close friends of Sen. John McCain (R-Ariz.) McCain's daughter Meghan McCain criticized President Donald Trump in her speech at her father's memorial service. "She is grieving for the father she adored. I think most Americans understand that," Graham said.

ESPN commentator Rob Parker has been suspended indefinitely as a result of disparaging racial comments he made about Redskins quarterback Robert Griffin III. Parker called his critics, among other things, “uneducated” and “silly.” Parker suddenly stopped tweeting on Thursday, presumably because his bosses at ESPN told him to knock it off.

Brazil nightclub fire kills at least 233 people in southern state of Rio Grande do Sul. Blaze ignited by sparks from pyrotechnics used by band for visual effects. Most of those who died were suffocated by fumes, fire brigade Sergeant Robson Muller says. Fire officials say at least one exit was locked and bouncers initially blocked patrons.

An orca named J35 has finally dropped her dead calf, which she'd been pushing with her head for at least 17 days. The sad spectacle was a prime example, and confirmation, of the complex emotional lives of these sophisticated cetaceans. Researchers worried that this "tour of grief" might seriously endanger the health of J35, but luckily, she appears to have made it through physically unharmed.

Mike Megna's kidneys are functioning at 45 percent, the bank has foreclosed on his West Milford home. "I'm leading my life like I'm rotting from the inside," he said. Megna was a Marine vet working as a Pompton Lakes police officer on the day of the terrorist attacks.

U.S. guidelines for diagnosis of Alzheimer's are being updated for the first time in nearly 30 years. The new definition includes patients with earlier stage symptoms and recognizes the condition as being on a continuum. Doctors hope to rely more on biomarkers, proteins and other molecules in patients' blood and tissue that are indicators of the disease.

Paul Ceglia, the 39-year-old western New York man who in 2010 sued Facebook and CEO Mark Zuckerberg for 84% of the company, has been indicted on federal charges of wire and mail fraud. He's scheduled to appear in Manhattan federal court on Wednesday, Nov. 28. At least a half dozen lawyers and firms have withdrawn as Cegia's attorney before Dean Boland.

Police fired warning shots to disperse hundreds of stone-hurling Afghans on Wednesday in the latest in a series of protests against Quran burning in the U.S. At least five people were wounded, two from gunshots. The topic of Quran burning has stirred outrage among millions of Muslims and others worldwide after a small American church in Florida threatened to destroy the holy book.

Frances Cobain is a guest vocalist on Amanda Palmer's new concept album, Evelyn Evelyn. Cobain's voice was mixed into a chorus with those of "Weird Al" Yankovic, Tegan and Sara and Gerard Way from My Chemical Romance. Palmer was impressed with Cobain for more than her singing.

News was confirmed following an archaeological dig which also unearthed evidence of frogs' legs being eaten in Britain 8,000 years before France.

If, however, the better shelter is only five minutes away,. individuals should move there immediately and forego the closer but unsafe buildings altogether.

Bodies of Naftali Frenkel, Gilad Shaar and Eyal Yifrach found in West Bank. Israel launched more than 30 air strikes on the Gaza Strip overnight. Israeli PM Benyamin Netanyahu said: "Hamas is responsible and Hamas will pay" Hamas denies any involvement in the abduction and murder of the teenagers.

Mediterranean diet has been repeatedly linked to health gains, such as cutting the risk of heart disease. Its mix of vegetables, olive oil, fresh fish and fruits may stop our DNA code from scrambling as we age. Nurses who adhered to the diet had fewer signs of ageing in their cells.

Alaska Division of Elections says it has more than 20,000 absentee and questioned ballots left to process from Tuesday's primary election. Most are expected to be Republican primary ballots that will decide the too-close-to-call race between U.S. Sen. Lisa Murkowski and Joe Miller. Miller currently leads Murkowski by 1,668 votes.

Study by animal behaviour specialists at the University of Lincoln, UK, shows that while dogs perceive their owners as a safe base, the relationship between people and their feline friends appears to be quite different. Results of the study reveal that while cats might prefer to interact with their owner, they do not rely on them for reassurance when in an unfamiliar environment.

David Cameron heard humming as he walked back to No 10 on Monday. He had just announced that he would resign as prime minister on Wednesday. Some speculated that it sounded like the start of the West Wing theme. Others suggested it was a Winnie the Pooh-style ditty.

Leonardo DiCaprio will star in the long-in-development “The Devil in the White City” Martin Scorsese will directing for Paramount. The project has been in the works for more than a decade. Billy Ray, whose credits include “Captain Phillips” and ‘The Hunger Games,’ will write the script.

Recent complaints about the state of Apple and photography have compelled me to take a journey down the historical highway. Apple's cloud service suite is made up of many different parts and systems. While it's great when it works, it also has a history of being prone to hard-to-diagnose outages.

"Sin City: A Dame to Kill For," "Jersey Shore Massacre" and "Love Is Strange" are all R-rated films. CNN's John Sutter asks: What on earth is in them that so horrifies the MPAA? Sutter: If there's an equivalence among these three films, and their equal unsuitability for anyone under 17, it's lost on me.

Cobalt mining has not happened at any sort of scale in the United States for decades. But a handful of mining companies are now staking claims at sites in Idaho, Montana and Alaska in search of the silvery blue mineral. Cobalt is a key component in the lithium-ion batteries that power electronic devices and electric cars.

A capybara that has eluded capture for more than two weeks was spotted Friday morning by our very own Breakfast Television cameraman Bertram Dandy. One of the two missing capybaras was seen swimming at the south end of High Park, near The Queensway, and then clambering up a bank. “She was right there! And she was ninja-still. National Louis University will offer a Groupon for a graduate-level teaching course. The three-credit introductory course will cost $2,232 to $950. The deal is open to as many as 25 buyers, who must possess an undergraduate degree. Only 25 slots will be available and the deal will tip at 15.

In 1977 Jones escaped from the facility, the US Military's only maximum security prison. He spent the next 37 years on the lam.

World leaders rally around the U.S. after it launched a missile strike on a Syrian air base. Russia condemned the move as "aggression" and suspended crucial coordination with Washington. The overnight missile attack was condemned by his allies in Russia and Iran. The bombing represents Trump's most dramatic military order since taking office.

"Rough Night" is a bachelorette-party-from-hell thriller comedy that’s got some push and some laughs, despite its essentially formulaic nature. Scarlett Johansson, Kate McKinnon, Jillian Bell, Ilana Glazer, and Zoë Kravitz star.

But it was another aspect of the storyline that was messing with some viewers' smart speakers. Both Alexa and Google Home were featured in the episode, and the cartoon characters yelled commands at their models.

Michaela Myers says she was first groped by her supervisor after a crew pizza party. She reported the harassment to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the Forest Service’s parent agency. The Forest Service sent her a letter that said the investigation was complete, no misconduct had been found, and the case was closed.

Scientists had long believed the Earth was dry and desolate during that time period. The manufacturing sector and its workers have been hardest hit by the growth of Wal-Mart’s imports. China has achieved its growing trade surpluses by manipulating its currency.

Facebook surveillance was associated with greater current distress over the breakup, more negative feelings, sexual desire, and longing for the former partner.

Steve Vogelsang was a journalism instructor at Red River College from 2002 to 2011. The 53-year-old was the news director and longtime sports anchor at CTV Winnipeg. He and his wife moved from Winnipeg to Nelson, B.C., after he left his post in 2011. A former student he had dated was granted a protection order against him.

Anna Lushchinskaya, 40, has been charged with felony assault after an incident on a New York City subway train. She is seen on video shouting expletives, spitting at fellow passengers and attacking a woman with an umbrella and keychain. The video comes just a few months after a lawyer named Aaron Schlossberg was caught making a racially charged, anti-immigrant rant.

Choi Eun-hee, an iconic movie star of the '60s and '70s, has died at age 92. Born in Gwangju, Gyeonggi Province, in 1926, she began her film career in 1947. She rose to stardom for her lead roles in "The Sun Of Night" (1948) and "A Hometown in Heart" In 1954, Choi married Shin Sang-ok, a leading film director. In 1978, Choi was kidnapped by a North Korean secret agent and taken to North Korea.

Former U.S. president Jimmy Carter, 92, is in Winnipeg to help build a Habitat for Humanity home. A Habitat volunteer said he saw Carter collapse after he'd been working in the sun for about an hour. Carter is being rehydrated in hospital, and his wife is with him, Habitat says. The former president has told organizers he is feeling fine.

Matthew Matheny, 40, of Warren, Ohio, set off for a hike on Mount St. Helens last Thursday. Friends reported him missing after he failed to return, prompting a search. About 30 search-and-rescue personnel, assisted by helicopters, searched for him daily. Matheny was found below a different trail, authorities said.

Republican presidential candidate Mitt Romney drew jeers from black voters Wednesday as he criticized President Barack Obama. Romney told the annual meeting of the NAACP that backing him over the Democratic incumbent is in the best interest of their families. He acknowledged his Republican Party doesn't have a perfect record on race relations, but pledged during a sometimes rocky speech that he would work with black leaders to put the country back to work.

Researchers from Princeton University and Uppsala University in Sweden report on a new species. The arrival 36 years ago of a strange bird to a remote island in the Galapagos archipelago has provided direct genetic evidence of a novel way in which new species arise. The study comes from work conducted on Darwin's finches, which live on theGalapagos Islands.

Police arrested a woman who they say swallowed a ring to keep police from finding it. Significant geomagnetic activity is expected Friday and Saturday after a couple of large Coronal Mass Ejections, or solar flares, erupted from the Sun. 16 with alleged gang ties arrested in multi-agency sting.

The mogul reveals plans for international speaking engagements, more scripted shows and why she's passing on Broadway production 'night, Mother' By year's end, Winfrey’s Chicago-based Harpo Studios will close its doors, with the 26-year-old company's productions transitioning to OWN headquarters in Los Angeles.

Rocco Ritchie, 15, refused to leave his father Guy Ritchie’s home in London to celebrate Christmas with Madonna in New York. A New York judge ruled that the disgruntled teenager must return home to his mother before school begins in January. “Madonna pulls the strings, calls the shots,” a source close to Madonna told RadarOnline.

President Trump hosted a lunch with the leaders of seven African countries. The meeting focused on economic, humanitarian, and security issues. Trump: Africa has a tremendous business potential and representing huge amounts of different markets. The United States is proud to work with you to eradicate terrorist safe havens, he said.

Miss World will no longer feature a swimsuit round in their competition. In recent years, Miss World has emphasized their "beauty with a purpose" round. Last night, the 64th Miss World, Rolene Strauss of South Africa, was crowned winner. It marked the final event featuring contestants wearing bikinis.

Joseph Andrade, 44, and his 22-year-old son, Carlos, lost their lives soon after excusing themselves from the festivities by telling people they were going for a smoke. For some reason, the younger man, who was not known to use drugs, joined his father, a reputed addict, in taking some powerful opiates.

Donald Trump believes the world would be better off if dictators like Saddam Hussein and Moammar Gadhafi were still in power. "100%," Trump replied when asked that question in an interview with CNN's Jake Tapper. The GOP front-runner painted himself as a “great unifier.”

The Nobel committee is giving up trying to contact Bob Dylan about his recent Nobel Prize win. Speculation swirled Friday when mention of the Nobel Prize was scrubbed from the musician's website. Dylan's Nobel Prize for literature marks the first time the award has gone to someone who is mainly seen as a musician.

The overreaction to Conan O’Brien’s departure has been kind of astounding. He walked away from ‘The Tonight Show’ because he rightly or wrongly felt that moving the show half an hour later would destroy the show's integrity. Conan in his own way has come to represent the aggrieved, the injured, the wrongly terminated. We see Conan as a victim because we feel as though he wasn’t given a fair shot.

Jack Ma made the pledge when he met with then-President-elect Trump in January 2017. He said the jobs would be created by supporting more sales by U.S. small businesses on Alibaba’s e-commerce platforms. Ma said the waves of new tariffs imposed by Washington and Beijing in recent months have undermined the plan.

Salon presents its list -- all right, fine, my personal list -- of great trippy movies. "Fantasia" was the first (and so far only) Walt Disney film to prompt viewers to ask, "What am I looking at?" and "What does it mean?" Will you add your own picks to the Letters section?

South Korean cargo vessel is missing after losing contact in the South Atlantic. 22 crew members are unaccounted for, the foreign ministry confirmed. Two Filipino crew members floating in a life raft were rescued Saturday. South Korea has requested Brazil and Uruguay to aid in the search and rescue.

Georgia state Rep. Jason Spencer appeared on Sacha Baron Cohen’s new show. Cohen asked Spencer to learn techniques to guard himself against Islamic extremists. Spencer responded by yelling the n-word multiple times and thrusting his buttocks at Cohen. Spencer said he was told the video was intended to be an educational aid to train officials.

Campbell Soup is altering its famous broth. The new recipe appears first in a limited-edition line in cans festooned with Chewbacca. “We’re closing the gap between the kitchen and our plants,” said Denise M. Morrison, chief executive of Campbell.

Christian numerologist David Meade says Nibiru will strike Earth on Sept. 23, 2017. He points to the Book of Revelation, which he says describes the image that will appear in the sky. Meade’s prediction is based largely on verses and numerical codes in the Bible. NASA senior space scientist David Morrison debunked an apocalyptic claim as a hoax.

Four-year-old Eli Waller, of Hamilton Township, was kept home from school by his mother on Wednesday, Sept. 23, because he was developing a little bit of pinkeye. He was otherwise fine and had been in school on Sept. 21 and 22. The Mercer County medical examiner’s office on Oct. 4 listed Waller's cause of death as Enterovirus D68, or EV-D68.

"Little Fockers" stars Robert De Niro, Ben Stiller, Owen Wilson, Dustin Hoffman, Barbra Streisand, Blythe Danner, Teri Polo, Jessica Alba, Laura Dern. Movie is about a man who wants to become the "Godfocker" - the patriarch of the next generation of Byrnes and Focker.

Russian state-run television station Channel One has come under fire after airing what was reported to be an eyewitness account of a 3-year-old boy having been tortured and crucified by the Ukrainian military. Russian opposition leaders said Monday that there was no evidence that such a public execution had taken place in Slovyansk. Russian bloggers and opposition activists are accusing Channel One of manipulating its viewers' minds.

Police arrested Jelinajane Bedrijo Almario, whose 18th birthday was on July 1, in May 2016. She was tried as an adult on charges of human trafficking of a minor, sending threatening emails to a family member of one of the victims and making terrorist threats. Prosecutors argued she trafficked four girls between the ages of 14 and 15 for a few weeks.

The naturally-occurring protein, called cardiotrophin 1, also known as CT-1, can trick the heart into repairing damage and improving blood flow. Therapy using the protein will likely be ready for clinical trials in patients with right heart failure and myocardial infarction — heart attack.

Use this form to submit any information you have on the shooting that occurred at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida on February 14, 2018. You are limited to uploading 4 files. Motorists taunted a distressed woman as police tried to talk her down from a bridge. The M3 at Sunbury, Surrey was closed for more than two hours yesterday. While Surrey Police were at the scene, one Twitter user tweeted: “Tell her to get on with it. Bloody ruining everyone’s weekend. Sat in this for an hour and a half now” Another person suggested that police shoot the suicidal woman with a rubber bullet.

Greece's PM George Papandreou says he is handing over to a coalition that does not exist. He then fails to install an old-style politician and personal ally as premier. Papademos insisted that both the socialist and conservative parties sign written undertakings to support Greece's 130 billion euro ($176 billion) bailout.

NEW: U.S. diplomat Raymond Davis ordered to remain in custody for 14 more days. NEW: Davis' lawyer files petition calling for his immediate release. Shumaila Kanwal, wife of man shot by Davis, dies after eating rat poison. Davis says he shot two men in self-defense when they attempted to rob him.

Zimmerman used the name Joe G.' on the site. Zimmerman faced two felonies in 2005 for obstructing justice and battery on a law enforcement officer. The cases were reduced to misdemeanor simple battery, and he was left with no criminal conviction. Zimmerman took down his website, a Twitter account and any other social media accounts.

Busy Philipps claims James Franco physically assaulted her on the set of Freaks and Geeks. The actress wrote about the incident in an excerpt from her upcoming memoir, 'This Will Only Hurt a Little' A representative for Franco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Billy Joel Marries Alexis Roderick in Surprise Wedding at His Estate. The couple "surprised guests at their annual July 4th party by exchanging vows in front of their family and close friends," the singer's spokeswoman said. The intimate ceremony was presided over by New York Governor Andrew Cuomo.

New research shows male black widow spiders copulate with immature females. Males use fangs to cut through the female's exoskeleton to deposit sperm. The young females produce the male's offspring once they’ve matured. Normally, mature female widow spiders engage in sexual cannibalism.

The decision brings to 26 the number of states granted waivers. The Education Department began granting the waivers in February. The administration says the waivers are a temporary measure. Congress remains at a stalemate regarding an overhaul to former President George W. Bush's signature accomplishment, No Child Left Behind.

The annual Shark Week television marathon puts many marine biologists and shark enthusiasts on edge. We love that it draws attention to sharks and that it sometimes includes some real science and conservation. We hate the way it's done: maximum menace and blood, a two-note soundtrack and, occasionally, a gross indifference to facts.

U.S. Rep. Thad McCotter's presidential run fizzled last year. He turned to another aspiration: writing a TV show. "Bumper Sticker: Made On Motown" featured characters bearing the nicknames of his congressional staffers, his brother and a drunk, perverted "Black Santa" It features a cartoon intro and closing snippet with an Oldsmobile careening through Detroit.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak hands power to his vice president but retains his title. Move sets up another conflict with the opposition movement, which has called on supporters to gather for a huge protest Friday. The White House is now squeezed between Arab and Israeli allies, who have complained that Mr. Mubarak was pushing Mr. Obama too hard to step down.

A bedraggled cockatoo that was pictured stripped of its feathers in a cyclone-hit Australian forest has died. The bird - dubbed "Debbie", after the cyclone - was rescued among broken twigs in Queensland on Tuesday. A photograph of the bird, by the Townsville Bulletin's Alix Sweeney, became a ubiquitous image of the storm.

A Los Angeles street artist has announced that he will add the hacked photos of Jennifer Lawrence and Kate Upton to his upcoming show. The artist, known as XVALA, plans to print life-sized reproductions of the photos on canvas for his "No Delete" show at CACA's The Showroom in St. Petersburg, Florida.

Katharine F. Lemansky, 45, was charged with cruelty to animals by the Cary Police Department after she told police that the incident took place in North Carolina. The photo went viral after it was posted to her Facebook page under the name "Katie Brown" It appears the post has since been taken off the Facebook page.

Thirty-six states have increased the annual tax businesses pay to finance unemployment benefits. Hawaii's employers face an average increase to $1,070 from $90 per worker. Six states are scaling back or freezing benefits for the unemployed. So far, 25 states have borrowed more than $25 billion from the federal government.

Two D.C. lawmakers introduce a bill that would provide 16 weeks of paid leave. The bill would cover the birth, adoption, fostering or fostering of a child. The measure would work much like unemployment insurance. Private employers would pay into a new Family and Medical Leave Fund.

Self-driving cars are being hit surprisingly often by other drivers who are distracted and not paying attention to the road. Other drivers have hit us 14 times since the start of our project in 2009, and not once has the self-driving car been the cause of the collision. Millions of fender benders every year go unreported and uncounted.

List of nominees for the 89th annual Academy Awards presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Best Picture: "Arrival," ''Fences," ''Hacksaw Ridge," ''Hell or High Water," ''Hidden Figures," ''La La Land," ''Lion," ''Manchester by the Sea", "Moonlight" Best Actress: Isabelle Huppert, "Elle"; Ruth Negga, "Loving"; Natalie Portman, "Jackie"; Emma Stone, "La La land"

Law enforcement investigating death of great white shark at Aptos beach. Experts believe the shark was a juvenile, weighing about 500 pounds and eight feet in length. The shark was found with cuts and wounds around it's body. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife is handling the necropsy.

There are nearly 1 million women in farming, accounting for 30 percent of U.S. farmers. Unlike the Farmettes and Women’s Land Army that took over while men fought in World War II, women today see farming as both a mission and a passion. The number of woman-operated farms more than doubled between 1982 and 2007.

David Goodall, a 104-year-old botanist and ecologist, died Thursday at the Life Circle clinic in Basel, Switzerland. Swiss law allows assisted suicide for anyone who acknowledges in writing that they are taking their lives willingly. Six states in the U.S. have passed death-with dignity laws for terminally ill people.

Matt Sandusky is not part of the legal case against the former Penn State football coach and his adoptive father, Jerry Sandusky. But in many ways, Matt’s story has become intertwined in the saga. Matt lived with the Sanduskys through many of the years that abuse is alleged to have happened.

Debra Harrell, 46, let her 9-year-old daughter play outside alone at the park. The South Carolina child had a cellphone she could use to call her mother in case of emergency. Harrell was arrested for “unlawful conduct towards a child” and put in jail.

Scientists have identified and reconstructed what they say is the most likely common ancestor of the many species on the most abundant and diverse branch of that tree. The work appears to support the view that in the global extinctions some 66 million years ago, all non-avian dinosaurs had to die for mammals to flourish. Scientists had been searching for just such a common genealogical link.

Felicia "Snoop" Pearson, 31, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to distribute heroin. She was caught by a wiretap in a joint federal-state drug probe of an alleged drug gang. She received credit for time served and a suspended seven-year sentence. The actress, who originally pleaded not guilty, hasn't exactly changed her tune.

Roger Ebert, the popular film critic and television co-host, died on Thursday in Chicago. He was 70. No cause was specified, but he had suffered from cancer and related health problems since 2002. In 1975 he became the first film critic to win a Pulitzer Prize, for his Sun-Times reviews.

Researchers at the University of North Carolina scanned the brains of 106 ‘high-risk’ infants at age 6, 12 and 24 months using magnetic resonance imaging. 15 of the high-risk infants were diagnosed with autism at 24 months. The researchers also found brain changes between 6 and 12 months, before ASD symptoms appeared. The findings raise the prospect of diagnosing autism spectrum disorder months before children develop symptoms, a goal that has proved elusive.

Billionaire David Tepper is moving from New Jersey to Florida, taking his tax burden with him. New Jersey's struggling state budget projections rely on income taxes for 40 percent of revenue. The Sunshine State has one of the country's lowest tax burdens: it taxes neither personal income nor investments, and its corporate tax is 5.5 percent.

Chicago joins other cities in pledging to remain a sanctuary city for undocumented immigrants. The move is an act of defiance in the face of Donald Trump’s past promise to cut off those cities from federal funding. Aldermen are expected to call on Republican Gov. Bruce Rauner to pressure Trump to back off his vow to interfere with funding.

Lakers owner Jerry Buss has been hospitalized for a few months with an undisclosed form of cancer. Buss, 79, has spent time in the intensive care unit at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. Lakers star Kobe Bryant: "I'm just trying to stay, gotta stay positive"

CNN's coverage of the Steubenville Rape Case verdict is pissing everyone off. Newscaster Candy Crowley, general correspondent Poppy Harlow, and legal expert Paul Callan all did their very best to focus solely on the guilty verdict's repercussions on the two rapists. There's next to no coverage on the girl who was brutally raped; instead, they talk almost exclusively of the rapists.

Nastassja Kinski praises sister for reporting sex abuse. Klaus Kinski died in 1991 after a career making some of Germany's most notable films. His daughter Pola said she had been abused between the ages of five and 19 by the actor. The actress, 51, whose films include Roman Polanski's Tess and Paris Texas, said she was "deeply shocked"

Patent application says it aims to prevent some or all of the damage to any electronic device with a processor. System needs a sensor to detect when the device is falling and how it is positioned relative to the ground. Position and speed of falling could be measured using simple gyroscopes, accelerometers or position sensors. Data on how and when impact is going to occur is fed into a processor that must make a decision on how best to hit the ground to avoid damage.

Oprah Winfrey will speak exclusively with disgraced former cyclist Lance Armstrong. Armstrong is considering publicly admitting that he used banned performance-enhancing drugs and blood transfusions during his cycling career. The notion of Armstrong confessing on Oprah was pre-mocked nearly two years ago by the bike racers and cartoonists Andy Shen and Dan Schmalz in their cult comic strip.

The Senate introduced a bill Thursday that would give the president new trade powers. The bill would allow the president to present a final agreement to Congress for an up-or-down vote. A similar bill, drafted by Rep. Paul Ryan, is expected to be introduced in the House in the coming weeks.

Over the past 35 years, China has grabbed nearly the entire U.S. fireworks market. 98 to 99 percent of what consumers will buy this year is made in China. The trend won’t be changing anytime soon, fireworks industry experts said. The industry’s shift to Chinese production came about shortly after the United States and China reestablished trade ties.

The Phunky Elephant in Staten Island is known for its decadent after dinner creations like its Cookie Crumble Martini and Milky Way cocktail. The ‘Roofie Colada’ was a dessert-drink hybrid made with coffee ice cream, Kahlua, vanilla vodka, caramel, chocolate syrup, topped with donuts and whipped cream. The name is allegedly derived from a joke on the cartoon “Family Guy’

Bell’s Two Hearted Ale was named number one in the 15th annual Best Beers in America survey, conducted by Zymurgy magazine. “This is an incredible honor for us. We got our start as homebrewers,” said Laura Bell, CEO, Bell's Brewery.

Connecticut Supreme Court finds that the state can forcibly medicate a man accused of killing a Yale doctor. Mentally ill Doctor Lishan Wang does not want to take medication that could make him competent to stand trial. Wang is charged with shooting and killing Yale Doctor Vajindor Toor outside Toor’s home.

The European Union has been on the list of Nobel Peace Prize candidates. The decision to award the 2012 prize to the bloc is a tribute to the EU's international reconciliation work, says DW's Bernd Riegert. Critics often accuse the European Union of being too bureaucratic, too undemocratic and a faceless beast.

U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo will spend the night in Pyongyang, his first overnight stay in North Korea. He will try to agree on at least an initial list of nuclear sites and an inventory that could be checked against the available intelligence. North Korean officials have yet to demonstrate that in working-level talks, the intelligence officials said.

Web wide crawl with initial seedlist and crawler configuration from March 2011. This uses the new HQ software for distributed crawling by Kenji Nagahashi. The seed list for this crawl was a list of Alexa’s top 1 million web sites, retrieved close to the crawl start date. The scope of the crawl was not limited except for a few manually excluded sites.

Emilio Gómez Milán and Elvira Salazar López from the University of Granada used thermal imaging to prove anxiety makes the tip of the nose heat up. They have dubbed the newly-found phenomenon, discovered by using thermal imaging cameras on volunteers, 'The Pinocchio Effect' It is an homage to Italian writer Carlo Collodi's 19th century literary wooden character whose nose grew.

A new study by the University of Colorado at Boulder ranks Chicago as America’s funniest city. Researchers hailed Chicagoans for their witty banter and observational humor. Other cities in the Top 10 were: Boston, Atlanta, Washington, Portland, New York, Los Angeles, Denver, San Francisco and Seattle.

1,000 additional law enforcement officers are being deployed as a precaution. Authorities found a second device in Manhattan a few blocks away from the one that exploded and removed it. Surveillance videos show the same man near the site of the explosion and another location where a pressure-cooker device was found four blocks away.

New Jersey state Senate President Stephen Sweeney says he plans to introduce legislation prohibiting the playing of professional sporting events with replacement officials. The NFL is the same league that has sued New Jersey to stop sports betting for a perceived threat to the integrity of the game. President Obama this afternoon was asked about the game’s ending: “Terrible,” he told reporters.

In new Vanity Fair article, Blackwater CEO Erik Prince reveals details on CIA assassination program. Prince: CIA did not inform its own station chief that the team was in the country. As recently as two months ago, Prince and a team were overseeing intelligence missions in Iran. In Washington, Prince has become a scapegoat for some of the Bush administration's misadventures.

Two inmates on an "honor block" used tools to cut their way out of the maximum security prison. The two inmates, Richard Matt, 48, and David Sweat, 34, used a small electrical saw, powered by extension cords. A massive manhunt continues in the heavily forested areas around the prison in Dannemora.

The race between Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump has tightened. Clinton, whose lead over Trump exceeded 8 percentage points at her peak following the Democratic convention, is ahead by 4 or 5 percentage points today, according to our polls-only forecast. The tighter margins in the polls reflect a loss of support for Clinton along with a modest improvement for Trump.

Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia talks with CNN's Piers Morgan Tonight. Scalia says he was dismayed by recent criticism of Chief Justice John Roberts. Scalia: "I'm not 'pro' death penalty, I'm 'anti' the idea that is not ultimately a democratic choice" He says he agrees with Bush v. Gore decision that Gore would have lost if all ballots were recounted.

Groupon was hit with its second lawsuit in as many months from employees who said they were screwed out of their overtime. This comes shortly after the online discounter lost its COO, its sales chief, its IPO date, and its favorite accounting metric. The latest blow comes from a federal class action suit just filed in Chicago, covering 50 "deal vetters"

Sergio Marchionne told Wall Street analysts on Wednesday that the company's chances of hitting 2018 financial targets are “significantly greater than 50 percent” The targets from Fiat Chrysler’s five-year plan ending in 2018 were initially set in 2014 and updated in January 2016. They include 136 billion euros of revenue and adjusted net profit of between 4.7 billion euros and 5.5 billion euros.

Alaina Marie Limpert, 25, was booked on one count of child abuse. Her almost-two-year-old daughter had ingested THC butter while eating macaroni and cheese with her father. THC is a chemical in cannabis that gets you high. Neither parent took the child to immediate emergency care, according to the police report.

NEW: Euric Cain, 21, is wanted in connection with the shooting, police say. NEW: A $12,500 reward is being offered for any information on Cain or the shooting. Tulane University is even offering up a $10,000 reward to anyone who can help crack the case. Peter Gold, 25, is in "guarded" condition at the hospital.

Officer Michael Doherty, 40, of South Boston, was placed on paid administrative leave after his arrest on charges of assault and battery and of using a motor vehicle without authority. Doherty's ex-girlfriend, Mary Niland, 24, had a brief unrelated hearing in the same courtroom prior to Doherty’s arraignment.

Jackson Odell was found unresponsive in his Tarzana residence in San Fernando Valley June 8. The cause of death has not been released, pending an autopsy. Odell had credits on “The Fosters,’ “Modern Family,” and “iCarly.”

Artificial sweeteners linked to weight gain and an increased risk of diabetes, Canadian study finds. Researchers at the University of Manitoba conducted a meta-review of 37 previously published studies. Only seven of the 37 studies they reviewed were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) The other 30 studies were longer and followed the participants for an average of 10 years.

Cybersecurity researcher Krzysztof Szczypiorski used club music to send Morse code-like messages. The messages were hidden in nearly imperceptible changes in tempo. To decode the messages, you could use an algorithm that analyzes the beats per minute.

British restaurant chain Pret a Manger says a second customer has died after eating a sandwich containing an allergen. The coffee-and-sandwich business has promised to improve its labeling. Natasha Ednan-Laperouse, 15, died in 2016 after eating Pret baguette that contained traces of sesame.

The Senate passed a massive tax overhaul early Saturday morning. The bill included about $1.4 trillion in tax cuts. It would lower the corporate rate to 20% from 35%, reshape international business tax rules and temporarily lower individual taxes. It was adopted on a 51-50 vote after Vice President Mike Pence broke a tie.

A 6.5 magnitude earthquake struck Eureka at around 4:30 p.m. Saturday. The quake, which lasted for around 30 seconds, had power poles waving back and forth. Fortuna seemed fairly undamaged as of early evening. Crews from Mendocino and Sonoma counties were on their way to help as late as Sunday night.

A mountain lion broke into a Colorado home and killed the cat named Klondike. The mountain lion ran out of the house and then made its way up into the wilderness near Boulder Canyon. Police say the homeowner returned Thursday night and found the mountain lion inside. It appeared that it had pushed through a screen and couldn’t get back out.

Undergraduate tuition and fees will go up 2.3 percent -- or by about $300 -- this fall. Room and board costs are also going up about 2.6 percent under the plan. The Rutgers Board of Governors unanimously approved the tuition hike. The 15-member board also approved a new $3.8 billion budget for the university.

The Labor Department announced that the economy produced 160,000 new jobs in April. Economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal had predicted 205,000 jobs added and expected the 5% figure. Hourly earnings, meanwhile, showed signs of life and grew 2.5% over the past 12 months.

NEW: Death toll rises to 153, with dozens still in critical condition. NEW: The dead included men, women and children, a hospital official says. The disaster came on the eve of the Muslim holiday of Eid al-Fitr. The tanker was driving from the southern port city of Karachi to Lahore.

A video shows a passenger being violently removed from a United Airlines plane in Chicago. The airline’s initial response to the publicity already has left it covered in shame. United CEO Oscar Munoz then made things worse with a statement of Orwellian doublespeak. The episode says more about the terms and conditions of air travel in the U.S.

Proposed peak season entrance fees and revised fees for road-based commercial tours would generate badly needed revenue for improvements to the aging infrastructure of national parks. During the peak season at each park, the entrance fee would be $70 per private, non-commercial vehicle, $50 per motorcycle, and $30 per person on bike or foot. If implemented, estimates suggest that the peak-season price structure could increase national park revenue by $70 million per year.

NEW: Amtrak engineer Brandon Bostian is interviewed for the first time since the derailment. NEW: He says he has "no recollection" of anything that happened once the train passed the station. The NTSB will reassemble the train to connect its brake lines and test the braking system. Eight people were killed and more than 200 were injured.

Ricky Gilmore, 49, is being treated for acute kidney failure from dehydration, a sprained wrist and a blood infection. He was found along a seldom-traveled road on the Navajo Nation about 10 miles from his home in Newcomb. Gilmore said he was dropped in the desert by a couple in a white truck whom he met while he was hitchhiking.

Wildlife officials moved in after complaints from tourists and concerns for their welfare. The "Tiger Temple," in Kanchanaburi Province west of Bangkok, has long been popular with tourists. The temple has been criticized by animal rights activists because of allegations it is not properly set up to care for the animals.

Mariah Carey & Nick Cannon Divorce 'A Done Deal' Separated for months. Ronnie Magro and Sammi Giancola have called it quits for good. Meg Ryan and John Mellencamp have ended their relationship as quietly as they began it.

Lauren Mann, 25, had been living in the Austrian capital and was working as an au pair, or nanny, for a local family. Police and firefighters who forced open her door Tuesday evening found the half-naked body on a mattress in the bedroom. U.S. authorities have identified her as Lauren Mann. Mann graduated in 2012 from the University of Colorado-Boulder's College of Music.

Norway will be the first country to completely transition to digital radio. The switch-off will start on January 11, at exactly at 11:11:11 AM local time. It’s cheaper to transmit via DAB (digital audio broadcasting) than FM, by about eight times. Many citizens are against the switch.

Wang Mingqing and his wife Liu Chengying lost their daughter Qifeng in 1994. She wandered off while they were running their fruit stall in Chengdu, Sichuan. The couple abandoned their stall to search for their daughter, but for years their efforts appeared to be in vain. In 2015 Wang became a taxi driver and enlisted the help of his customers. He asked them to post appeals on social media in the hope his missing daughter might see them. Two weeks ago a 27-year-old woman in Jilin province contacted the Wangs via social media after reading about his search and realising she might be the girl in question. A DNA test confirmed she was Wang’s daughter.

White House officials offered few details and no timeline for a possible attack on Syria during a 90-minute conference call on Thursday evening. Members issued statements afterward reiterating their long-held views on Syria. The call appears to have done little to change anybody’s mind.

Almost six million Adelie penguins are living in East Antarctica, more than double the number previously thought. Research by an Australian, French and Japanese team used aerial and ground surveys, tagging and resighting data and automated camera images. They focused on a 5,000 kilometre stretch of coastline, estimating it was home to 5.9 million birds. On this basis, they estimate a likely global population of 14 to 16 million.

The United States will not recognize the result of Venezuela's presidential election. U.S. Deputy Secretary of State John Sullivan said a response to Sunday's vote would be discussed at a G20 meeting in Buenos Aires on Monday. Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro was seeking a six-year term in a Sunday election boycotted by the opposition and condemned by foes as the “coronation” of a dictator.

She is accused of killing daughters Nika, 5, and Michaela, 1, at their Benbrook, Texas home. More than 3,000 people have been rescued, Houston's mayor says. The Coast Guard is getting 1,000 calls per hour, an official says. A mandatory evacuation order is issued for the city of La Grange, Texas. The National Weather Service says the storm is expected to linger for days.

Officials say a mix up occurred when the boxes were moved from the school's guidance office to the shipping area.
